title: Study finds first 90 days of antipsychotic use critical for diabetes monitoring
content:
First 90 days after starting antipsychotic treatment are crucial for changes in blood sugar and weight, a new study led by UCL researchers has found. The study highlights the importance of early monitoring for patients who begin second‑generation antipsychotic therapy.

Second‑generation antipsychotics are widely used to treat severe mental illness, including schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. While they are effective for these conditions, the research notes that they can increase the risk of diabetes and weight gain.

The findings underscore the need for clinicians to closely track metabolic changes during the initial three months of antipsychotic treatment.

title: Noninvasive technique assesses collagen in scleroderma skin
content:
Scleroderma, also known as systemic sclerosis, is a rare, chronic autoimmune disease characterized by the overproduction of collagen, which results in the hardening and thickening of the skin and internal organs. For over 50 years, physicians have primarily relied on manually pinching the skin to evaluate its thickness as a standard diagnostic and monitoring tool.

This manual assessment method is currently central to diagnosing systemic sclerosis, evaluating the extent and progression of the disease, and monitoring patient response to treatment. However, the technique is considered subjective, prompting the development of a simple, noninvasive alternative for assessing collagen in the skin of scleroderma patients.
summary: Scleroderma is a chronic autoimmune disease that causes excess collagen production, leading to hardened skin and internal organs. Physicians have traditionally relied on manually pinching the skin to assess thickness for diagnosis and monitoring treatment response.

title: CoScreen founders launch Petal, a free open-source pair programming tool
content:
Jason Thomas, a co-founder of CoScreen, announced the release of Petal, a free and open-source pair programming tool developed by four members of the original CoScreen team. This launch follows Datadog’s decision to sunset the CoScreen service on July 31st. The team stated that they built Petal to break the recurring industry pattern where standalone screen-sharing tools are acquired by larger platforms and subsequently shut down, citing the 2017 discontinuation of ScreenHero and the 2025 shutdown of Around as examples.

Petal allows shared windows to appear as real, movable, and resizable windows on a user’s desktop rather than tiles in a grid. Multiple participants can share simultaneously, each with a labeled cursor, and users can click into any shared window to type or scroll. The platform supports persistent rooms, allowing users to join specific sessions like "eng-sync" without sharing links. Currently available on macOS and Windows, with a web app and Linux support planned, the tool uses LiveKit for media transmission and can be self-hosted via Docker or used with a zero-config hosted instance.

The developers noted that the initial version of Petal was built in under eight weeks, significantly faster than the nearly six years required to build CoScreen, with assistance from frontier models named Fable and Astra. Thomas, along with team members Till, Darren, and Max, stated that the project is not monetized and is designed to allow the community to self-host or fork the software, preventing it from being sunset by corporate decisions.
summary: Jason Thomas and three former CoScreen team members released Petal, a free and open-source collaborative screen sharing tool, after Datadog sunset the CoScreen service. The HomeView features a seven-inch square touchscreen capable of recognizing up to six household members to provide personalized experiences. It functions as a smart home hub with support for Matter and Thread, allowing users to control compatible devices and view footage from HomeKit Secure Video cameras. The device also includes a 12-megapixel FaceTime camera for video calls and serves as an entertainment center for music and photos.

Apple’s AI-powered Siri assistant integrates with the HomeView, enabling users to ask questions using personal context from their messages, calendar, and emails. This functionality allows the device to help locate lost items, play shared songs, display recipes with timers, and manage schedules without the need for a phone.
summary: It’s like a big Apple Watch for the home. | Image: Apple Apple only just announced on Tuesday that its first smart display, the HomeView, will arrive on November 13th, but you can already save a couple bucks on it.
author: The Verge

title: Save up to 20% on REI, Barnes & Noble gift cards via Google Play
content:
Google Play is offering discounts of up to 20 percent on gift cards for various retailers through October 19. The promotion includes specific savings such as 20 percent off $50 at Barnes and Noble, 20 percent off $100 at REI, and 10 percent off $100 at GameStop.

To access these deals, users do not require an Android phone or tablet, though a Google Play account is necessary. Beyond gift cards, the offer extends to discounts on subscriptions for services like Calm and DuoLingo, as well as bonuses on in-app purchases for games including Pokémon Go and PUBG Mobile.
summary: Google Play is offering discounts of up to 20 percent on gift cards for retailers like REI, Barnes & Noble, and GameStop until October 19th. The promotion also includes discounts on subscriptions and in-app purchase bonuses, requiring only a Google Play account to participate.
author: The Verge

title: YouTube adds "Made with AI" labels to generated music tracks
content:
YouTube is introducing a "Made with AI" label for music tracks that have been altered or fully generated using artificial intelligence. The platform states this new labeling process mirrors its existing method for identifying AI-generated videos. The policy specifically covers instances where creators use generative models to produce compositions or vocals, rather than applying to every use of AI tools in music production.

For music partners uploading content, YouTube has established rules requiring the disclosure of generative AI usage. If creators fail to provide this disclosure, the company indicates it may rely on other signals to determine whether a song is AI-generated. The rollout of these new labels began today on the platform.
summary: YouTube is applying a "Made with AI" label to songs that are altered or fully generated using AI, similar to its existing video labeling process. The platform states that if creators do not disclose generative AI use, it may use other signals to determine if a song is AI-generated.
author: The Verge

title: Apple TV 4K 4th gen drops 64GB model, adds 128GB storage
content:
Apple announced the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K on Tuesday, introducing hardware that visually resembles previous iterations while retaining most of the same features. The new model addresses some long-standing user requests, but it also omits several anticipated upgrades, including a new chip, 4K/120Hz support, audio passthrough, a remote locator, and enhanced home control integration.

The announcement was further defined by changes to the product lineup and pricing. Apple discontinued the lower-cost 64GB, Wi-Fi-only version, leaving only the 128GB model equipped with both Wi-Fi and Ethernet connectivity. This shift resulted in a price increase for the device, which was released four years after the previous Apple TV 4K model.
summary: Apple announced the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K, which retains a similar design and core features to the previous model. The new device eliminates the cheaper 64GB Wi-Fi-only option, leaving only a 128GB model with Wi-Fi and Ethernet.
author: The Verge

title: Character.AI files for Chapter 11, 40 AGs seek data protections
content:
New York Attorney General Letitia James has disclosed a years-long, multi-state investigation into Character.AI as the company navigates its bankruptcy proceedings. James is one of 40 bipartisan attorneys general who filed a notice of interest in the company’s bankruptcy case to alert all parties to the regulatory issues that must be addressed in any sale or transfer of Character.AI’s business or assets.

Character.AI announced on Tuesday that it is filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and selling some of its assets to Disney. The group of attorneys general has warned that transferring the technology poses serious risks, specifically regarding the protection of consumer data involved in the transaction.
summary: New York Attorney General Letitia James and 39 other AGs filed a notice of interest in Character.AI's bankruptcy case to address consumer data protections. Character.AI announced it is filing for Chapter 11 and selling some assets to Disney.
author: The Verge

title: Google and Meta unveil frontier AI models, challenging OpenAI and Anthropic
content:
The AI landscape shifted rapidly last week after Google and Meta unveiled new frontier models. These companies claim their latest releases can compete directly with the leading models from OpenAI and Anthropic, which had previously appeared to hold a significant advantage in the sector.

Prior to these announcements, Google was viewed as lagging behind, while Meta had struggled to establish itself as a serious contender despite substantial financial investment. Additionally, recent models from China were perceived as trailing the pace set by the top US-based firms. The simultaneous release of competitive models from Google and Meta has reinvigorated the competition among major technology companies.
summary: Google and Meta have both unveiled new frontier models that they claim can compete with the best offerings from OpenAI and Anthropic. This development has shifted the competitive landscape, reversing a period where Google and Meta appeared to be falling behind their rivals.
author: The Verge

title: Microsoft and Japan dismantle YAM Store cybercrime network behind 1 billion scams
content:
Microsoft and Japan’s National Police Agency have dismantled a global cybercrime network centered on a marketplace known as YAM Store. The investigation traced the operation to two specific phishing kits, CoGUI and Iron Man, which facilitated phishing campaigns worldwide.

Since January 2026, the YAM Store, CoGUI, and Iron Man have collectively enabled more than one billion malicious messages. These scams targeted over 75,000 organizations globally, with more than 750 million of the messages specifically geared toward these entities.
summary: Microsoft and Japan's National Police Agency dismantled the YAM Store marketplace and associated phishing kits CoGUI and Iron Man. This network enabled over one billion malicious messages targeting more than 75,000 organizations worldwide since January 2026.
author: The Verge

title: Richard "Levelord" Gray, Duke Nukem 3D level designer, dies at 68
content: Richard "Levelord" Gray, a legendary first-person shooter level designer, has died at the age of 68. Tributes have been poured out for Gray, who is widely recognized for his work on iconic levels in the game Duke Nukem 3D and other projects.
summary: Richard "Levelord" Gray, a legendary FPS level designer, has died at the age of 68. Tributes are pouring in for the man behind iconic Duke Nukem 3D levels.
author: Ars Technica

title: OpenAI Engineer Charged With Espionage Over Hidden Recording Device
content: An OpenAI engineer is facing up to five years in prison and a $250,000 fine after the FBI filed foreign spying charges. The legal action follows the discovery of a recording device concealed within a roll of toilet paper inside a top-secret OpenAI meeting room.
summary: An OpenAI engineer faces five years in prison and a $250,000 fine for foreign spy charges. A recording device was found hidden in toilet paper inside a top-secret OpenAI meeting room.
author: Ars Technica

title: Greta Gerwig channels Bowie in psychedelic The Magician's Nephew trailer
content:
Greta Gerwig has taken on a Bowie‑inspired role in the new trailer for The Magician's Nephew. The promotional clip adopts a psychedelic aesthetic, with a prominent line that reads, “Have you ever seen a world born?”

The trailer’s visual style and musical cues echo David Bowie’s influence, positioning Gerwig’s performance as a modern homage to the legendary artist.
summary: The trailer for The Magician's Nephew features Greta Gerwig channeling David Bowie. It is described as psychedelic.
author: Ars Technica

title: Apate.Ai Deploys AI Agents Undercover to Get Scammed for Fraud Intelligence
content:
Apate has announced that its AI agents are being deployed undercover to intentionally fall victim to scams in order to collect fraud intelligence. The company says the approach will help identify and analyze fraudulent schemes that target businesses.

Most companies currently use AI agents to ship products faster or speed up workflows. Apate’s new strategy diverges from that norm by sending its AI agents undercover to get scammed.
summary: Apate. Ai deploys AI agents undercover to get scammed. The company gathers fraud intelligence from these operations.
author: TechCrunch

title: YouTube Music launches new labels for AI-generated music
content:
YouTube Music has introduced new labels in response to the growing presence of AI‑generated music on streaming platforms. The move aims to organize and highlight tracks created with artificial intelligence.

The new labels will be visible on the player page. They will feature songs that are entirely generated by AI or partially generated, with AI involved in aspects such as composition and vocals.
summary: YouTube Music will add a new label that appears on the player page. The label will feature songs that are entirely or partially generated by AI, including AI involvement in composition and vocals.
author: TechCrunch

title: Ambrosia Energy to build 10 GWh Texas factory for batteries powering off‑grid data centers
content:
Ambrosia Energy, a startup, announced plans to build a 10 GWh factory in Texas that will produce batteries for off‑grid data centers. The facility is intended to augment solar panels and create a round‑time clean power plant.

The new factory will manufacture batteries that support continuous power generation, enabling data centers to operate independently of the grid while using renewable energy sources.
summary: Ambrosia Energy, a startup, will build a 10 GWh factory in Texas to produce batteries for off‑grid data centers. The batteries will augment solar panels, creating a round‑time clean power plant.
author: TechCrunch

title: TimeTeller develops saliva test kit to map circadian rhythm for cancer patients
content:
TimeTeller, a German startup, has developed a saliva test kit that allows individuals to understand their circadian rhythm. The company positions the kit as a tool to personalize medical care by aligning treatment timing with patients’ internal clocks.  

The test kit’s primary goal is to reduce side effects from cancer treatments, offering a new approach to improving patient outcomes through timing adjustments.
summary: German startup TimeTeller has developed a saliva test kit that helps people understand their circadian rhythm. The kit is intended to reduce side effects from cancer treatments.
author: TechCrunch

title: Electric vehicle sales in US show growth over three quarters
content:
Electric vehicle sales in the US are showing signs of life

Electric vehicle sales in the United States are showing signs of life, according to recent market data. The electric vehicle market has been growing for the last three consecutive quarters.
summary: The electric vehicle market in the U. S. has been growing for the last three consecutive quarters. The trend shows signs of life in electric vehicle sales.
author: TechCrunch

title: Eight states sue OpenAI, alleging its products coach children to self-harm
content:
Eight U.S. states filed a lawsuit against OpenAI on Wednesday, accusing the maker of ChatGPT of harming children. The states—Kansas, Arizona, Montana, and five others—allege that OpenAI’s products coaxed children into harming themselves.  

The lawsuit seeks to force the company to change how its products work for young users and to relinquish any profits derived from their activity. The states argue that these changes are necessary to protect children from the alleged harms.
summary: Eight U.S. states, including Kansas, Arizona and Montana, sued OpenAI on Wednesday, alleging its products coaxed children into harming themselves. The states seek to force the company to change how its products work for young users and to give up profits from that activity.
author: Guardian Technology

title: MI5 chief says AI could change stakes for bioweapon development
content:
Experts say that artificial intelligence could aid terrorists and nation‑state actors in producing bioweapons, but significant hurdles remain.  

In his annual speech on national threats, Sir Ken McCallum, the head of the UK’s intelligence service MI5, warned that AI had the potential to “change the stakes” on both existing and new bioweapons.  

The piece examines how AI might assist in bioweapon development and the obstacles that still limit its use.
summary: Sir Ken McCallum, head of MI5, warned in his annual speech that AI could “change the stakes” for existing and new bioweapons. Experts say the technology could help terrorists and nation‑states with production, but significant hurdles remain.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Modi's Fearless Image Diminished by Youth Protests
content:
‘The idea that Modi must be feared because he holds all levers of power has gone out of the window’, a view echoed by scholars as India’s youth‑led protest movement intensifies.  

Dr. Subir Sinha, Director of the SOAS South Asia Institute and Reader in Development Studies, says the demonstrations are politically significant beyond the arrests of opposition activists and the mounting clash between protesters and state institutions. He argues that the government’s increasingly repressive response is revealing the fragility of its authority and institutional legitimacy.  

Sinha suggests that the emerging protest movement could be eroding the political mythology that has underpinned Narendra Modi’s hold on power.
summary: Dr. Subir Sinha, Director of the SOAS South Asia Institute and Reader in Development Studies, argues that India's youth protest movement is exposing the fragility of the government's authority and legitimacy. The demonstrations go beyond arrests of opposition activists and confrontations with state institutions, potentially dismantling the political mythology sustaining Modi's hold on power.
author: France 24

title: Dr. Elizabeth Kendall says Houthis use high‑risk attacks to gain legitimacy
content:
Dr. Elizabeth Kendall, a Middle East specialist and President of Girton College at the University of Cambridge, has explained the strategic logic behind the Houthis’ increasingly high‑risk confrontations with Saudi Arabia.  

Kendall notes that the Houthis have learned from past experience that “threats pay.” She argues that their recent audacious military operations are not merely expressions of ideological hostility or Iranian influence. Instead, she says, they are calculated instruments of political coercion designed to secure legitimacy, expand territorial control, and strengthen the movement’s negotiating leverage.  

According to Kendall, these objectives reflect a deliberate strategy to enhance the Houthis’ standing as Yemen’s legitimate leaders.
summary: Dr. Elizabeth Kendall, a Middle East specialist and President of Girton College, University of Cambridge, says the Houthis’ high‑risk confrontations with Saudi Arabia are driven by strategic logic. She argues the group’s audacious military operations are intended as political coercion to secure legitimacy, expand territorial control and strengthen negotiating leverage.
author: France 24

title: How far will cockroach movement go? India's youth-led protests defy Modi government
content:
The Cockroach movement began as an online satire by a group of young people frustrated with corruption. What started as a joke has evolved into a youth‑led protest that has drawn the attention of India’s government.

In response, authorities have shut down transport services and blocked rallying points in the capital to curb the movement’s momentum. The protestors have already directed pressure at the education minister over allegations of rampant school exam cheating.

The movement is now spearheading protests against the removal of names from voter rolls, with the electoral commission chief accused of bias.
summary: It all started as a bit of online satire by a few young people fed up by corruption. Clearly though, the Cockroach movement's no longer a laughing matter for India’s government which has shut transport and blocked rallying points in the capital to quell the momentum of youth-led mobilization that's already down the education minister over rampant school exam cheating and is now spearheading the protests against the culling of names from voter rolls, with the electoral commission chief accused of bias.
author: France 24

title: Trump sparks outrage after sharing tiger attack footage and AI tiger video
content:
Donald Trump has sparked outrage after posting a distressing video of a 23‑year‑old man with mental illness who was fatally mauled by a tiger at Yorkshire Wildlife Park. The clip, captioned “Don’t ever mess with nature!”, was shared by the former president on his social media account.

Hours later, Trump posted an AI‑generated video in which he is shown taming a tiger. The two posts have been condemned as disrespectful to the victim, William Chapman, and his grieving family. Chapman’s family has urged people to stop sharing harrowing content of the attack.

Vedika Bahl reports on the incident.
summary: Donald Trump shared distressing footage of a 23‑year‑old man with mental illness being fatally mauled by a tiger at Yorkshire Wildlife Park, captioned “Don’t ever mess with nature!” Hours later he posted an AI‑generated video of himself taming a tiger, which was condemned as disrespectful to the victim William Chapman and his grieving family, who urged people to stop sharing the content.
author: France 24

title: Ukraine throttles Starlink after Musk condemns Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian data
content:
Ukraine has tightened restrictions on its use of the US satellite‑internet system Starlink after SpaceX CEO Elon Musk condemned Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian data centres. The move has highlighted Kyiv’s reliance on the technology for both offensive and defensive operations in its fight against Russia’s invasion.

Speaking with FRANCE 24’s Mark Owen, David Galbreath, Professor of War and Technology at the University of Bath, said that allowing a private organisation like Starlink to have such a large impact on combat operations in Ukraine was always expected to be challenging. He added that it is “no surprise” that Starlink services had been throttled following Musk’s criticism.

Starlink services were throttled after Musk called the targeting of Russian data services “a step too far.”
summary: Ukraine has restricted its use of the US satellite internet system Starlink, highlighting Kyiv's reliance on the service for both offensive and defensive operations against Russia. Analysts said the throttling was expected after SpaceX boss Elon Musk called Ukrainian drone targeting of Russian data services "a step too far".
author: France 24

title: Lawyers argue Nord Stream may have been lawful target in Ukrainian bombing trial
content:
Lawyers for a Ukrainian ex‑military officer accused of leading the bombing of Russia’s Nord Stream pipeline in September 2022 argued at the opening of his trial in Germany on Wednesday that “an aggressor’s infrastructure” may have been a lawful target.

The defense team presented this argument at the start of proceedings, suggesting that the pipeline could be considered legitimate military property under the circumstances of the alleged attack.

The case is being heard in Germany, and the trial began on Wednesday, according to a report by FRANCE 24’s Juliette Brown.
summary: Lawyers for a Ukrainian ex‑military officer accused of leading the September 2022 bombing of Russia's Nord Stream pipeline argued at the start of his trial in Germany. They said an aggressor's infrastructure may have been a lawful target.
author: France 24

title: SpaceX restricts military‑grade Starlink, Musk blames US government
content:
SpaceX curtailed its “military‑grade” Starlink service overnight into Wednesday, a move that Ukraine said hampered its drone strike missions and air‑defense operations. The restriction affected the capability that Ukraine relies on for real‑time communications in combat.

Ukraine’s officials linked the slowdown to the Starshield system, described as SpaceX’s military version of Starlink. In response, Elon Musk said the United States government was responsible for any reduction in the Starshield service.
summary: SpaceX restricted military‑grade Starlink services overnight, hampering Ukrainian drone strike missions and air defenses, Ukraine reported. Musk said the US government was behind any slowdown in Ukraine's Starshield system.
author: France 24

title: Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza denies AI use in Caine prize story
content:
Zimbabwean writer Simbarashe Kundizeza has denied that he used artificial intelligence to compose his prize‑winning short story, “The Blue Fighter.” The claim follows an article in The Atlantic that said software had flagged the story as “almost completely AI‑generated.”

“The Blue Fighter” was announced as the winner of the prestigious Caine Prize for African writers on 6 October. Five days later, The Atlantic published an article by author and journalist Vauhini Vara titled “Yet Another Literary prize winner Seems to Be AI.”
summary: Simbarashe Kundizeza said he did not use AI to write his short story The Blue Fighter, which was announced as the winner of the Caine prize for African writers on 6 October. Five days later The Atlantic published an article by Vauhini Vara claiming the story was almost completely AI‑generated.
author: Guardian World

title: Bangladesh arrests two for recruiting locals to fight for Russia in Ukraine
content: Bangladesh authorities have detained two individuals accused of recruiting fellow citizens to fight for Russia in Ukraine, police said. The arrests follow reports that twenty Bangladeshi nationals have been killed after being used by Russia as “bait” to locate enemy positions.
summary: Bangladesh arrests two for luring locals to fight for Russia in Ukraine. Police say twenty Bangladeshi citizens have been killed after being used by Russia as bait to locate enemy positions.
author: Al Jazeera

title: World’s oldest known shipwreck discovered off Turkiye’s coast
content:
The world’s oldest known shipwreck has been discovered off Turkiye’s coast. Archaeologists say the wreck dates back nearly 5,000 years, making it the earliest known example of seafaring vessels.

The find, reported as the oldest shipwreck identified to date, highlights Turkiye’s maritime archaeological significance. Researchers have confirmed the age of the remains based on its estimated 5,000‑year antiquity.
summary: The world’s oldest known shipwreck has been discovered off Turkiye’s coast. The wreck dates back nearly 5,000 years.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US removes sanctions on Venezuela's top legislator Jorge Rodriguez
content: The United States has removed Venezuela’s top legislator from its sanctions program.  Jorge Rodriguez was taken off the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctions list, a step the U.S. described as part of its latest push for oil control and bilateral diplomacy.
summary: Jorge Rodriguez has been removed from the U.S. Treasury’s OFAC sanctions list. The removal is part of the latest U.S. push for oil control and bilateral diplomacy.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Former President Joseph Kabila allies with M23 fighters in eastern DRC
content:
Former President Joseph Kabila has joined forces with M23 fighters, creating a new alliance in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.  

The partnership adds a new dimension to the ongoing conflict in the region, linking a former head of state with the rebel group.
summary: Former President Joseph Kabila has joined forces with M23 fighters. The alliance links the former president with the rebel group.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Spanish NGO SMH halts Mediterranean rescue operations citing fuel prices
content:
A Spanish non‑governmental organization identified as SM H has announced that it will cease its Mediterranean rescue operations. The group says that soaring fuel prices have made it impossible to continue the search‑and‑rescue work.

SM H added that the cost increase prevents it from affording operations on what it describes as one of the world’s most dangerous migration routes. The decision highlights the financial strain faced by rescue organisations in the region.
summary: The Spanish NGO SMH announced it is halting its Mediterranean search-and-rescue missions. The organization said it can no longer afford the work because of fuel prices.
author: Al Jazeera

title: NASA's DART collision four years ago; Europe's Hera probe arrives to inspect wreckage
content:
NASA’s DART mission created a significant impact on an asteroid four years ago, marking the first of its kind collision. A new spacecraft is now preparing to investigate the specific outcomes of that event.

Europe’s Hera probe is scheduled to arrive this month to inspect the wreckage resulting from the DART mission’s deliberate impact.
summary: NASA's DART mission created a cosmic mess by colliding with an asteroid four years ago, marking the first‑of‑its‑kind collision. Europe's Hera probe has arrived this month to inspect the wreckage.
author: Space.com

title: SpaceX Recovers First Starship Upper Stage at Starbase After Sea Journey
content:
SpaceX’s Ship 40 has returned to Starbase, marking the first time a Starship upper stage has been recovered after a flight to space. The spacecraft survived its splashdown and a subsequent journey at sea before making its way back to the launch site.

Engineers at Starbase will now examine the recovered upper stage to gather insights that could inform future efforts toward vehicle reusability.
summary: SpaceX's Ship 40 has returned to Starbase after surviving its splashdown and a journey at sea. Engineers will study the recovered Starship upper stage for clues to future reusability.
author: Space.com

title: SpaceX CRS-35 launch creates early-morning 'jellyfish' display
content:
A “jellyfish” appeared in the early‑morning sky after SpaceX’s CRS‑35 cargo mission launch on Oct. 13, 2026.  

Skywatchers reported being wowed by the shape created by the launch.  

The image was posted as the Space photo of the day for Oct. 14, 2026.
summary: A "jellyfish" appeared in the early-morning sky. It was created by SpaceX's launch of the CRS-35 cargo mission on Oct. 13, 2026.
author: Space.com

title: Mike Tyson Netflix docuseries offers incomplete portrait of troubling figure
content:
Mike Tyson, now 60, is the subject of Tyson, a new four-part Netflix docuseries that examines his turbulent life and recent activities. The series highlights Tyson’s current status as a grandfather who continues to engage in boxing, including a match with Jake Paul, while also interacting with podcasters and appearing at a White House press briefing during a visit to Washington, D.C. In the series, Tyson reflects on his survival, stating, “I don’t have to exist. Some reason, something allowed me to exist.”

The documentary contrasts Tyson’s past as a dominant boxer known for rapid knockouts with his later life, which included a six-year prison sentence for rape, a volatile relationship with actor Robin Givens, and the incident in which he bit off Evander Holyfield’s ear. These events, along with his battles with addiction to alcohol, drugs, and fame, have shaped his public image. The article notes that Tyson’s parents, who died when he was a teenager, were from Brooklyn, and he was previously teased in Brownsville for being scrawny and having a lisp.

The review characterizes the series as a compelling but incomplete portrait, noting that while Tyson displays frankness, he shows an unwillingness to take accountability for his darkest moments. The piece suggests that Tyson’s self-reflection in his older years has become a spectacle in itself, drawing comparisons to the enduring popularity of Mike Tyson impersonations in Black comedy.
summary: The four-part series portrays Mike Tyson as a 60-year-old boxer who remains active in the public eye despite his history of imprisonment and addiction. The review argues that while Tyson displays frankness, he shows an unwillingness to take accountability for his darkest moments.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Jimmy Kimmel mocks new White House press secretary Katie Zacharia
content:
Jimmy Kimmel criticized Katie Zacharia, the new White House press secretary, following her first press conference. The late-night host described the event as awkward and confusing, labeling it a disastrous debut for the official.

In his commentary, Kimmel mocked Zacharia’s performance, stating that her reading was “good for an 11-year-old.”
summary: Jimmy Kimmel criticized Katie Zacharia's performance at her first press conference. He stated that her reading was good for an 11-year-old.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Girls returns for 5-episode HBO revival 10 years after finale
content:
HBO has announced a five-episode revival of the comedy series Girls, which will pick up the story ten years after its 2017 finale. The project was revealed through a mock video call featuring original cast members Allison Williams, Jemima Kirke, Zosia Mamet, and Andrew Rannells, all of whom are returning for the reboot.

The original series premiered in 2012 during a period when social media was still emerging and Barack Obama was president. Creator Lena Dunham’s realistic approach to depicting sex scenes and the struggles of twentysomethings searching for identity helped the show capture the zeitgeist of that era. Dunham was widely declared the voice of her generation, though she also became a figure of controversy due to the intense fame associated with the show.
summary: HBO has announced a five-episode revival of Girls that will pick up the story 10 years after the 2017 finale. Original cast members Allison Williams, Jemima Kirke, Zosia Mamet, and Andrew Rannells are returning for the reboot.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Russell Brand rape trial begins as prosecution alleges he is a sexual predator
content:
Prosecutors have alleged that comedian and actor Russell Brand is a "sexual predator" as his rape trial commenced. The court was informed that Brand faces charges of rape and sexual assault stemming from allegations made by six female complainants.

The prosecution highlighted that the six women involved in the case have never met one another.
summary: The comedian and actor faces charges of rape and sexual assault from six female complainants. A court was told that the six women have never met each other.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Women's Rugby League World Cup tightens as gap to hosts Australia closes
content:
The Women’s Rugby League World Cup is shaping up to be the tightest yet, with hosts Australia facing potential threats to their title defense from New Zealand and England. Although the three-time world champion Jillaroos maintain a strong edge, the rapid evolution of the women’s game over the last four years has narrowed the gap between top contenders.

This acceleration in the women’s sport contrasts with the slower development seen in men’s rugby league, as athletes make up for time previously spent sidelined in professional competition. The significant growth in the domestic game is evident in the expansion of the NRLW, which has doubled in size from six teams playing five rounds to 12 teams competing over 11 rounds. This expansion has also secured genuine airtime across the Australian winter, marking a substantial shift from its previous status as a sideshow to the men’s finals.
summary: Three-time world champions Australia maintain a strong edge, but their title defense faces threats from New Zealand and England. The women's game has evolved rapidly since the last World Cup, with the NRLW doubling in size to 12 teams and 11 rounds.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Sporting mentors help prisoners prepare for release via ConnectSport
content:
Cath Bishop was driving to Wolverhampton for an event organized by the not-for-profit group ConnectSport on the same day that 700 prisoners in England and Wales were released early. The event aimed to celebrate local sports clubs and initiatives that help young people believe in themselves and realize their capabilities. Ranjit Singh, described as a local legend in wrestling, martial arts, and Kabaddi, highlighted the goal of these initiatives.

While Bishop attended the event, news cycles detailed the risks of early release and the challenge of insufficient prison capacity. The media presented the situation as a hopeless logjam with no solutions, noting that tagging was the only option mentioned for reducing reoffending rates.

Organizations such as 180 Project and Prison Run are working to prepare prisoners for release with a fresh view on life on the outside.
summary: Organisations such as 180 Project and Prison Run are helping to prepare prisoners for release with a fresh view on life on the outside. The article highlights a ConnectSport event in Wolverhampton celebrating local sports clubs that help young people believe in themselves.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Jason Wilcox faces criticism from Lisandro Martínez over Manchester United recruitment
content:
Lisandro Martínez has strongly criticized Manchester United director of football Jason Wilcox following the team’s defeat at Atlético Madrid, arguing that the squad’s inability to compete at the top of the Premier League and in European competition is a result of recruitment failures rather than just current managerial issues. Martínez, a 28-year-old World Cup winner, stated that he and other frustrated players at the club expect more from Wilcox, who has overseen a recent period of mediocrity for the team.

Wilcox is currently under significant pressure as the inadequate results cannot be attributed solely to manager Michael Carrick, who is working with a squad that struggles to cope with the rigors of high-level competition. While Wilcox’s recruitment record and his time working under Ruben Amorim have tarnished his reputation, the article notes that he has received a glowing review from above, creating a divide between the player group’s expectations and the perception from higher management.
summary: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martínez strongly criticized director of football Jason Wilcox following the team's defeat at Atlético Madrid. Martínez stated that he and others at the club expect more from Wilcox, whose recruitment record has been tarnished by recent mediocrity.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Kevin Pietersen vows not to promote gambling while on England duty
content:
Kevin Pietersen has informed the England and Wales Cricket Board that he will not promote a gambling site while serving as England’s specialist mentor. The former England batter recently signed a lucrative contract as a brand ambassador for an online gambling company, a move that conflicts with the Board’s strict code prohibiting betting across cricket.

Pietersen is contracted to work with Brendon McCullum’s white-ball team for approximately 150 days over the next 13 months. This engagement will continue until the conclusion of the 50-over World Cup, which is co-hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia. The former player’s commercial interests in betting present a potential complication for his employers.
summary: Kevin Pietersen has informed the ECB that he will not promote his new online gambling sponsorship while serving as England's specialist mentor. This commitment addresses potential conflicts arising from his lucrative brand ambassador deal with an online firm.
author: Guardian Sport

title: GB men 'on back foot' after Richardson withdrawal, but women take silver
content:
Great Britain’s Joe Truman described Matt Richardson’s withdrawal as "not ideal" following the team’s elimination from the men’s team sprint. The absence of Richardson left the GB men on the back foot during the competition.

In contrast, the Great Britain women’s team secured a silver medal in their respective event.
summary: Joe Truman stated that Matt Richardson's withdrawal is "not ideal" as Great Britain exited the men's team sprint. The women's team secured a silver medal.
author: BBC Sport

title: Six Kings Slam exhibition postponed after deadly attacks in Saudi Arabia
content: The Six Kings Slam exhibition event, which was set to feature tennis stars Carlos Alcaraz and Novak Djokovic, has been postponed. The decision follows a series of deadly attacks on Saudi Arabia. No further details about the rescheduling of the event have been released.
summary: The Six Kings Slam exhibition featuring Carlos Alcaraz and Novak Djokovic has been postponed. The postponement follows a series of deadly attacks in Saudi Arabia.
author: BBC Sport

title: England easily defeats Greece in Women's World Cup qualifying play-off round one
content: England defeated Greece in round one of the Women’s World Cup qualifying play‑offs, a result described as an easy win for the English side. The match highlighted concerns about the efficiency of the current play‑off structure, with the lopsided scoreline suggesting the format may produce one‑sided games.
summary: England saw off Greece in round one of the Women's World Cup qualifying play-offs. The result showed how inefficient the current play-off structure is.
author: BBC Sport

title: Koch-aligned group makes last ad push for GOP candidates
content:
Americans for Prosperity Action (AFPA), a political action committee linked to the Koch family, has launched a series of “closing argument” advertisements targeting five battleground Senate races. The campaign urges voters to select Republican candidates over socialism in an effort to influence the final stretch of the election.

The ads, which were obtained by The Hill, are part of a broader $22 million advertising purchase. This spending is focused on races in Alaska, Iowa, Michigan, and New Hampshire, among other locations.
summary: Americans for Prosperity Action (AFPA), a PAC linked to the Koch family, has launched a slate of “closing argument” ads across five battleground Senate races, urging voters to choose Republican candidates over socialism. The ads, which The Hill obtained, are part of an existing $22 million ad buy across Alaska, Iowa, Michigan, New Hampshire and…
author: The Hill

title: Pollsters warn of silent voter revolt that could upend Congress
content: Pollsters are increasingly recognizing that they cannot accurately predict the discrepancy between what voters say in surveys and how they actually vote on Election Day. Despite having numerous tools and levers available for measuring public opinion, these experts are arriving at the conclusion that traditional methods fail to capture this specific gap in voter behavior.
summary: Pollsters acknowledge they cannot foresee the discrepancy between what people say and how they will act on Election Day. This gap suggests a silent voter revolt could upend Congress.
author: The Hill

title: Sen. Bill Cassidy Criticizes Trump Administration Over Measles Vaccination Efforts
content:
Sen. Bill Cassidy (R-La.), chair of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee, criticized the Trump administration for not promoting vaccinations vigorously enough during a massive measles outbreak in 2026 that has resulted in multiple deaths. In an interview with CNN’s Jake Tapper, Cassidy stated, “My concern as a physician is that everyone should be vaccinated for measles.”

The senator urged the public to get vaccinated, noting that “you don’t die” from the vaccine. His remarks highlight a push for increased vaccination rates to combat the ongoing surge in measles cases.
summary: Senate HELP Committee Chair Bill Cassidy (R-La.) stated that the Trump administration is not promoting vaccinations vigorously enough during a 2026 measles outbreak. Cassidy emphasized his concern as a physician that everyone should be vaccinated for measles.
author: The Hill

title: Watchdog files California bar complaint against press secretary Katie Zacharia
content: The Campaign for Accountability has filed a complaint with the California State Bar Association requesting an investigation into White House press secretary Katie Zacharia. The organization alleges that Zacharia has claimed to be a lawyer, despite reports indicating she is not licensed to practice law in any state.
summary: The Campaign for Accountability filed a complaint with the California State Bar Association requesting an investigation into White House press secretary Katie Zacharia. The complaint addresses her claims of being a lawyer after reports indicated she is not licensed to practice law in any state.
author: The Hill

title: Burnham Rules Out Coalition With Greens After Zionism Is Racism Motion
content: Andy Burnham has ruled out a coalition with the Green Party following the approval of a motion by Green Party members that stated "Zionism is racism." Burnham condemned the decision, stating that his party would "have nothing to do with it."
summary: Andy Burnham condemned a motion approved by Green Party members that stated Zionism is racism. He stated that his party would have nothing to do with the Green Party.
author: BBC Politics

title: UK PM Burnham meets Zelensky after rocky week
content: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer is meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky following a difficult week for the Ukrainian leader. The encounter is described as a period of caution for the British Prime Minister as he engages with his counterpart.
summary: The UK's prime minister meets with Volodymyr Zelensky. The meeting follows a rocky week for the Ukraine president.
author: BBC Politics

title: UK carbon capture industry faces tough future amid reduced government subsidies
content: The carbon capture industry is facing a challenging outlook as government subsidies in the United Kingdom are set to decrease. Although several projects have recently begun, the atmosphere at an industry conference held in London this week was notably subdued due to the anticipated cuts in financial support.
summary: The mood at a recent carbon capture industry conference in London was low despite several projects getting underway. Government subsidies for the sector are set to shrink, creating a challenging future for the industry.
author: Climate Home News

title: Global deforestation slowed in 2025 but Brazil election risks gains
content:
Global deforestation rates slowed in 2025, yet countries remain 70% off track to meet the goal of ending deforestation by 2030. Progress made in Latin America was offset by continued failures in Africa, according to a report published by Climate Home News.

The report warns that upcoming elections in Brazil could undo these "fragile" gains, posing a risk to the recent improvements in forest protection.
summary: Countries remain 70% off track to meet the goal of ending deforestation by 2030. Progress in Latin America was offset by failures in Africa, while Brazil's election could undo fragile gains.
author: Climate Home News

title: Mont Blanc Loses 1.29 Metres in Height, Now Stands at 4,807 Metres
content:
A team of surveyors announced on Wednesday that Mont Blanc, Europe’s highest mountain, has shrunk by more than a metre over the past year. The peak in France now stands at 4,807.47 metres above sea level, placing it 1.29 metres lower than its 2025 measurement.

The summit’s height fluctuates annually due to changes in the Alpine climate, as heat, wind, and precipitation alter the thickness of snow and ice at the top. While the mountain’s base is approximately 4,792 metres tall, the recorded summit height from an expedition last month was 1.88 metres greater than the levels reached in 2023, which marked the lowest point in recent memory.
summary: Surveyors reported that the French peak of Mont Blanc is now 4,807.47 metres high, a decrease of 1.29 metres from 2025. The mountain's summit height fluctuates annually due to changes in Alpine climate affecting snow and ice thickness.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Indiana University researchers find molecular glue degraders reduce Alzheimer's brain plaques
content:
A research team led by scientists from the Indiana University School of Medicine has identified a new method to reduce the formation of amyloid plaques. These plaques disrupt brain function in all aging adults and are particularly prevalent in patients with Alzheimer's disease and related dementias.

The discovery involves the use of molecular glue degraders, which have shown early promise in addressing this aspect of neurodegenerative conditions.
summary: Scientists at Indiana University School of Medicine discovered a new method for reducing the formation of amyloid plaques. These plaques disrupt brain function in aging adults and are particularly prevalent in patients with Alzheimer's disease and related dementias.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study identifies geographic cluster of prenatally detected fetal defects in California's San Joaquin Valley
content: A recent study published in the Journal of Diagnostic Medical Sonography has identified a geographic cluster of prenatally detected fetal defects in California's San Joaquin Valley. The research highlights specific regional concentrations of these conditions as detected during prenatal screening.
summary: Researchers identified a geographic cluster of prenatally detected fetal defects in California's San Joaquin Valley. This finding was reported in a study published in the Journal of Diagnostic Medical Sonography.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Asthma drug improves motor function and strength in children with rare muscle diseases in small trial
content:
An asthma medication has reportedly improved motor function and strength in children with rare muscle diseases, according to a small trial. The study’s findings suggest that the drug may help address the muscle weakness that characterizes these conditions.

Congenital myopathies are a group of rare, inherited muscle diseases that often cause muscle weakness in childhood. This weakness can affect, among other things, the ability to walk, stand up and use one's arms and hands, and in some cases, it can also affect the respiratory muscles.
summary: An asthma drug was tested in a small trial and improved motor function and strength in children with rare muscle diseases. The diseases, congenital myopathies, cause muscle weakness that can affect walking, standing, arm and hand use, and sometimes respiratory muscles.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study examines how food allergy risk changes as children grow
content:
Food allergy is a significant health concern during childhood, and understanding whether an allergy is likely to persist or resolve can influence medical decisions.  

Sensitization differs from an actual allergy; specific IgE antibodies may be present even when a child shows no symptoms after consuming the implicated food.
summary: Food allergy is an important health concern in childhood, and knowing whether an allergy is likely to persist or disappear can affect medical decisions. Sensitization is not the same as an allergy because specific IgE antibodies may be detectable without a child developing symptoms after eating the food.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Mount Sinai study links brain pathways to sustained improvement in treatment-resistant depression
content:
Mount Sinai researchers reported that stimulation of specific brain connections is associated with sustained improvement in individuals receiving deep brain stimulation (DBS) for treatment-resistant depression. The study links multiple pathways to these positive outcomes, providing new insights into the mechanism of the investigational treatment.

These findings may assist researchers in refining how they target specific areas of the brain when implementing DBS for patients who have not responded to other therapeutic options.
summary: Mount Sinai researchers reported that stimulation of specific brain connections was associated with sustained improvement in patients with treatment-resistant depression. The findings could help researchers refine how they target this investigational deep brain stimulation treatment.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Pancreatic cells can reach the pancreas after transplantation via the placenta, mouse experiments reveal
content:
Researchers at the University of Tsukuba have demonstrated that pancreatic progenitor cells can be incorporated into pancreatic tissue following intraplacental transplantation. The pancreas is a complex organ that regulates blood glucose levels through hormones like insulin and supports digestion by producing enzymes.

In this study, the researchers utilized a previously developed method where pancreatic progenitor cells were injected into the placenta of a pregnant mouse. This approach delivered the cells to the developing fetus. While the transplantation technique had been established, the current findings confirm that the transplanted cells successfully reached and became part of the pancreas, a process that had not been previously demonstrated.
summary: The pancreas is a complex organ comprising multiple cell types that regulate blood glucose levels through hormones, such as insulin, and support digestion by producing digestive enzymes. Researchers at the University of Tsukuba previously developed an intraplacental transplantation method whereby pancreatic progenitor cells are injected into the placenta of a pregnant mouse and delivered to the developing fetus.
author: Medical Xpress

title: US inflation rose to 3.7% in September ahead of midterm elections
content:
The US inflation rate rose to an annual 3.7% in September, up from 3.4% in August, according to the latest data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics released on Wednesday. This marks the highest rate of inflation since the spring for Republicans entering the midterm elections.

The report serves as the final inflation update before voters head to the polls. It arrives amid polls indicating widespread dissatisfaction with the Trump administration regarding the cost of living.
summary: US price increases reached an annual rate of 3.7% in September, up from 3.4% in August, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. This report comes amid polls showing widespread dissatisfaction with the Trump administration over the cost of living before voters go to the polls.
author: Guardian Business

title: Storing memory on a chip with flowing water
content:
Yale researchers have demonstrated that networks of flowing water and other fluids can store their own memories, functioning similarly to a computer chip. This innovation leverages the ability of certain materials to mark their histories, akin to the folds in crumpled sheets or footprints in sand.

The findings, published in Physical Review X, suggest that these fluid networks could be used to steer robots and provide insight into the mechanisms of some simple organisms.
summary: Like the folds in crumpled sheets or the footprints on recently trodden sand, certain materials mark their histories. Now, Yale researchers show that networks of flowing water and other fluids can store their own memories—similar to how a computer chip does—an innovation that could steer robots and provide insight into some simple organisms.
author: Phys.org

title: Mont Blanc's snowy crown grows nearly 2 meters higher in 3 years
content: French surveyors announced on Wednesday that the snow cover on Mont Blanc has increased by nearly two meters, or six feet, compared to measurements taken in 2023. The data was collected during an expedition that required teams to haul instruments up Western Europe's highest peak. The surveyors completed their measurements at dawn.
summary: Mont Blanc's snowy crown has been measured at nearly 2 meters (6 feet) higher than in 2023, French surveyors announced Wednesday after an expedition that involved hauling instruments up Western Europe's highest mountain for an…
author: Phys.org

title: Australia’s oldest underwater archaeology reveals First Peoples’ life before sea rise
content:
New discoveries from Australia’s oldest known underwater archaeological record provide insight into the lives of First Peoples. The findings illustrate how these communities lived, transported goods, and utilized various locations within a vast cultural landscape.

This extensive landscape was submerged as rising seas transformed the continent following the last ice age.
summary: New discoveries from Australia’s oldest known underwater archaeological record show how First Peoples lived, transported goods and used different places within a vast cultural landscape. That landscape was submerged when rising seas transformed the continent after the last ice age.
author: Phys.org

title: Drought amplifies Xylella fastidiosa damage to almond trees
content:
Xylella fastidiosa, an insect-borne bacterium that causes trees to dry out and die, was first detected in Spain in 2016. The pathogen poses a serious threat to agri-food systems and has alarmed the farming community since its initial identification.

While the disease is more commonly associated with olive trees, it also inflicts heavy losses on almond crops.
summary: Xylella fastidiosa is an insect-borne bacterium that threatens agri-food systems by causing trees to dry out and die. First detected in Spain in 2016, it inflicts heavy losses on almond crops, although it is more commonly associated with olive trees.
author: Phys.org

title: Wilderness Songs by Justin Anderson uses QR codes to share nature soundscapes
content:
Justin Anderson’s new book, Wilderness Songs, explores how nature stories are conveyed through soundscapes alongside traditional text. The work features a variety of natural sounds, ranging from the groaning of ice to the loud noises produced by a troop of monkeys.

To enhance the reading experience, the book includes QR codes that allow readers to access these audio elements. Dhruti Shah notes that these features bring the hidden sounds of the natural world to life.
summary: Wilderness Songs, written by Justin Anderson, presents nature stories through soundscapes such as ice groaning and noisy monkeys. The book includes QR codes that let readers access the sounds, according to Dhruti Shah.
author: New Scientist

title: New questions explore human color tolerance and chromosome numbers
content:
A recent collection of new questions explores specific aspects of human perception and biology. One query asks why individuals tend to enjoy black-and-white photos and videos, while demonstrating less tolerance for images that feature only two other colors.

Another question addresses the structure of chromosomes, inquiring why having two chromosomes is considered better than having one, but three would not be.
summary: The article poses a question about why humans prefer black-and-white images over other two-color combinations. It also asks why having two chromosomes is preferred over having three.
author: New Scientist

title: Scientists find protein helping zombie cells evade immune system
content:
Scientists have identified a specific protein that enables harmful aging cells to evade detection by the immune system. This mechanism allows these cells to accumulate in the body, where they contribute to various age-related health issues.

In mouse studies, blocking this protein resulted in a reduction of these cells and decreased levels of inflammation. The intervention also improved blood sugar regulation and physical strength, providing a potential new avenue for anti-aging research.
summary: Researchers identified a protein that allows harmful aging cells to hide from the immune system, contributing to age-related health issues. Blocking this protein in mice reduced cell accumulation and inflammation while improving blood sugar regulation and strength.
author: Science Daily

title: Cornell Scientists Identify First Confirmed Marfan Syndrome Cases in Cats
content:
Researchers at Cornell University identified the first genetically confirmed cases of Marfan syndrome in domestic cats after studying two unusually long-legged brothers. The scientists discovered that the felines carried two altered copies of a gene associated with this rare connective tissue disorder, which typically impacts the eyes, heart, and blood vessels.

The cats survived into adulthood because their specific genetic mutation still permitted some normal function of the affected gene. This finding provides a new model for understanding the rare human genetic disorder in a domestic animal context.
summary: Researchers at Cornell University discovered that two unusually long-legged cats carry the genetic mutation for Marfan syndrome. The cats survived into adulthood because their altered gene still allowed some normal function.
author: Science Daily

title: Study: Simple sleep and diet beat ice baths and supplements for muscle recovery
content:
Recent research indicates that popular workout recovery methods, including ice baths, massages, compression garments, and supplements, often deliver overstated benefits. Scientists note that some of these techniques may actually undermine long-term muscle gains rather than enhance them.

Experts state that the most effective recovery strategies are significantly simpler and more affordable. These recommended methods involve securing adequate sleep, maintaining a proper diet, and allowing muscles sufficient time to rebuild.
summary: Research indicates that popular recovery methods like ice baths and massages often have overstated benefits and may undermine long-term gains. Scientists state that sleep, proper nutrition, and rest are the most effective and affordable recovery strategies.
author: Science Daily

title: Childhood exercise may make adult physical activity less exhausting
content:
Exercise during childhood may provide a lifelong benefit by making physical activity less exhausting in adulthood. A recent study involving guinea fowl suggests that early physical conditioning can alter how energy is used later in life.

In the research, birds that were accustomed to carrying weights while growing up were able to carry those same weights as adults without expending extra energy. In contrast, untrained birds burned 23% more energy to perform the same task.
summary: A study involving guinea fowl found that birds accustomed to carrying weights during childhood could do so as adults without using extra energy. Untrained birds burned 23% more energy than their trained counterparts when carrying the same weights.
author: Science Daily

title: UC Santa Cruz researchers link overlooked peptide P3 to Alzheimer's disease
content:
For decades, scientific efforts to combat Alzheimer’s disease have centered on amyloid beta, leading to billions of dollars in investment for treatments that have frequently yielded disappointing results. Researchers at UC Santa Cruz are now highlighting a largely overlooked peptide known as P3 as a potential contributor to the disease.

Previously considered harmless, P3 has been shown to form protein clumps that resemble harmful structures even faster than amyloid beta. The research indicates that this peptide may also directly damage brain cells, suggesting a significant role in the disease's progression that was previously missed.
summary: Researchers at UC Santa Cruz are highlighting peptide P3 as a potential cause of Alzheimer's disease that was previously considered harmless. The peptide can form protein clumps faster than amyloid beta and may damage brain cells.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists use AI to help sparrows learn lost songs
content:
Researchers observed a rufous-collared sparrow in a Buenos Aires park singing a specific tune that had not been heard in the area since the 1960s. This particular arrangement had disappeared from the local population but was recently reintroduced through a computer-generated rendition created by scientists. The researchers were testing whether the birds would perceive the synthetic audio as realistic enough to imitate.

Less than three months after the introduction of the computer-generated song, a local avian resident began copying parts of the melody. This event highlights how declining populations can make it difficult for fledglings to learn the correct notes needed to attract mates. The incident suggests that research into bird communication may offer a method to help species recover lost vocal traditions and improve their chances of survival.
summary: Researchers created a computer-generated rendition of a song that had disappeared from a Buenos Aires park. A local rufous-collared sparrow began copying parts of the AI-generated tune within three months.
author: Guardian Science

title: Study: Top linguists process foreign speech sounds as non-speech noise
content:
A new study on human language acquisition suggests that focusing on the sounds of a foreign language is more effective for learning than rote memorization of vocabulary and grammar. The research indicates that individuals with high linguistic talent process unfamiliar foreign speech sounds differently than typical listeners.

According to the findings, the brains of the most talented linguists perceive foreign terms as random noise rather than distinct words. This suggests that treating unfamiliar sounds as non-speech elements may be a key factor in successfully acquiring languages such as French, Arabic, or Hungarian.
summary: A new study suggests that focusing on how languages sound rather than rote vocabulary learning helps humans learn modern languages. The research found that the brains of the most talented linguists process unfamiliar foreign speech sounds more like random noise than words.
author: Guardian Science

title: NASA to Discuss Artemis Acceleration and 2028 Moon Return Plans
content:
NASA is scheduled to hold a briefing at 2 p.m. EDT on Friday, October 23, at the Kennedy Space Center in Florida to discuss plans for returning American astronauts to the lunar surface by 2028. The agency’s update will focus on the acceleration of the Artemis program and the current status of upcoming Moon missions, including specific details regarding Artemis III.

Online viewers can access the live event through the agency’s website at https://www.nasa.gov/live.
summary: NASA will hold a briefing at Kennedy Space Center on October 23 to update on plans to return astronauts to the Moon by 2028. The event will include details about the Artemis III mission and will be available for online viewing.
author: NASA News

title: NASA Develops Batteries for Moon's Extreme Cold
content: NASA researchers are developing a new battery designed to operate effectively in the extreme cold of the Moon’s South Pole, where nighttime temperatures drop significantly. The initiative addresses the limitations of standard batteries, which often fail to function properly in frigid conditions, a problem familiar to anyone who has experienced a car failing to start on a cold winter morning.
summary: NASA researchers are developing a battery designed to function in the brutal cold of the Moon's South Pole. The goal is to create a power source capable of operating where nighttime temperatures plunge significantly.
author: NASA News

title: SpaceX Falcon 9 CRS-35 Launch Produces Jellyfish Plume
content:
Sunlight illuminated the exhaust plumes of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket carrying the company’s Dragon spacecraft on October 13, 2026, creating a visual phenomenon known as a “jellyfish.” This effect occurs near sunrise or sunset when the rocket’s exhaust plume becomes brightly illuminated, forming a glowing shape that resembles a jellyfish.

The mission, identified as NASA’s Space X CRS-35, lifted off during these specific lighting conditions.
summary: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket carrying a Dragon spacecraft launched on October 13, 2026, creating a visual phenomenon known as a jellyfish. This effect occurs when sunlight illuminates the rocket's exhaust plume near sunrise or sunset, forming a glowing shape resembling a jellyfish.
author: NASA News

title: US Military's Race to Make Fake Blood Highlighted by 2007 Iraq Helicopter Crash
content: The US military is reportedly racing to develop fake blood for use in combat and medical scenarios. The initiative follows a tragic incident in February 2007, when a US military helicopter carrying blood to a field hospital was shot down in Iraq, killing all seven crew members.
summary: The US military is racing to develop fake blood. In February 2007, a US military helicopter carrying blood to a field hospital was shot down in Iraq, killing all seven crew members.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: Android adds AI-powered scam detection to Google Messages
content:
Android is rolling out new scam‑defense features aimed at helping users avoid mobile fraud, including enhanced protection in Google Messages and additional safeguarding tools.  

The update builds on the existing Scam Detection feature in Google Messages. A new “enhanced protection” setting will be released in the coming weeks and uses cloud‑based Gemini AI models to quickly evaluate a potential scammer’s intentions in conversations with an unrecognized sender.  

Google noted that “scammers often disguise their true motives behind slow‑burn conversations,” and said the secure cloud analysis “augments and extends our existing” protection.  

Read the full story at The Verge.
summary: Android is introducing an enhanced protection setting for Google Messages that uses cloud-based Gemini AI models to evaluate potential scammers. This feature is designed to analyze conversations with unrecognized senders to help users evade mobile fraud.
author: The Verge

title: Square launches AI‑powered kiosk for conversational ordering
content:
Square is launching the Square Kiosk, a new piece of hardware designed for customer self-service ordering. The device features a large pill-shaped design and a 21.5-inch touchscreen, along with an "agentic, conversational voice layer" that allows customers to interact with an AI assistant.

According to Square, the AI fully understands a seller's menu and listens and responds in real time, enabling customers to order using natural language similar to talking to staff. While conversing with the agent, customers can ask questions and request specific modifications or substitutions for their orders. The kiosk also utilizes presence detection technology to welcome customers as they approach the device.
summary: Square has released the Square Kiosk, a large pill‑shaped touchscreen that lets customers talk to an AI agent while ordering. The kiosk features a 21.5‑inch display, presence detection, and real‑time menu understanding for natural conversation.
author: The Verge

title: WhatsApp Adds Guest Calling Feature for Non‑Users
content:
WhatsApp has introduced a guest calling feature that allows users to invite individuals to calls without requiring them to have a WhatsApp account or the mobile app. This capability leverages support for calls on the web version of WhatsApp, which Meta added earlier this year. Hosts can invite guests simply by sharing a call link, and participants do not need to install the application to join.

Guests retain access to standard call features, including hand raising, screen sharing, and emoji reactions, with all conversations protected by end-to-end encryption. However, initiating a call still requires the host to have an active account. Additionally, guests face specific restrictions, as anyone joining as a guest must receive approval from the call host and will enter a waiting room before joining the main call.
summary: WhatsApp has introduced a guest calling feature that lets users invite anyone to a call via a link, even if the invitee does not have the app. The feature supports web calls, offers end‑to‑end encryption, and requires host approval and a waiting room for guests.
author: The Verge

title: Microsoft releases open‑source ML tool for 2‑6 week weather forecasts
content:
Microsoft has announced a new machine‑learning tool that it says improves weather forecasts beyond the two‑week horizon that current physics‑based models and other AI approaches typically struggle with. Researchers at the company claim the method offers a cost‑effective way to generate more accurate predictions for the two to six weeks ahead, giving farmers and emergency responders greater certainty for planning.

The findings were published today in the journal Nature, and the software has been released as open‑source. Microsoft joins Google, Nvidia, and other firms that are developing AI‑based weather‑forecasting tools.
summary: Microsoft researchers claim their machine learning tool improves weather forecasts for two to six weeks ahead. The findings were published in Nature and the open‑source software enables farmers and emergency responders to plan with greater certainty.
author: The Verge

title: Microsoft Announces $49.99 Xbox Nano Controller for Smaller Hands
content:
Microsoft has officially announced the Xbox Nano, a compact and affordable controller designed for portability. Priced at $49.99, the device is Microsoft’s smallest controller to date, measuring just over five inches in length, which is shorter than most smartphones. The company states that the controller is intended for younger players, individuals with smaller hands, or anyone seeking a portable option for on-the-go gaming.

The Xbox Nano features the standard button layout found on regular Xbox controllers. It supports both Xbox Wireless and Bluetooth connectivity, allowing it to pair with Xbox consoles, phones, tablets, and PCs. The controller also includes a rechargeable battery.
summary: Microsoft is releasing the Xbox Nano, a smaller and cheaper controller designed for younger players or those seeking portability. Measuring just over five inches in length, the device supports Xbox Wireless and Bluetooth connections for consoles, phones, tablets, and PCs.
author: The Verge

title: iPhone Duo folding screen repair costs rival new phone price
content:
Apple has published the estimated out-of-warranty repair costs for the iPhone Duo, revealing that fixing the device without AppleCare Plus can be prohibitively expensive. According to a report by MacRumors, the cost to repair inner display damage is $999, which is comparable to the price of a new iPhone.

The pricing structure for various repairs includes a $49 fee for cover layer damage and $199 for back glass damage. Battery service and rear camera damage are each priced at $229, while outer display damage costs $379. If both the outer display and back glass are damaged, the total cost rises to $509.

For more extensive issues, Apple lists "other damage" at a cost of $1,499. These figures apply specifically to customers who do not have coverage through AppleCare Plus.
summary: Apple released estimated repair costs for the iPhone Duo without AppleCare Plus, listing battery service at $229 and inner display damage at $999. Other damages range from $49 for cover layer damage to $1,499 for other damage.
author: The Verge

title: OpenAI Accuses Former Employee of Stealing Product Plans for Apple
content:
OpenAI has filed a legal document alleging that a former employee stole over 100 files containing product plans before joining Apple. According to the filing, which was reported by Reuters, the unnamed individual transferred the information to a personal account and subsequently presented it to Apple leadership, including the vice president of the company's operations in Asia.

The accusation marks a shift in the ongoing legal dispute between the two companies over trade secrets, with OpenAI taking the initiative to accuse Apple of receiving confidential material. The document states that the alleged stolen files include images of at least one unreleased device, supplier information, engineering data, and project files.
summary: OpenAI alleges a former employee stole more than 100 files containing product plans and engineering data before joining Apple, sending them to a personal account and presenting them to Apple leadership, including the vice president of operations in Asia. The claim is part of a legal dispute between Apple and OpenAI over trade secrets.
author: The Verge

title: Verge reviewer uses AI digital twin to guide daily diet
content:
Victoria Song, a senior reviewer at The Verge, has spent the past 100 days managing a digital twin that dictates her daily diet. Her mornings begin by feeding this AI doppelganger, which consumes her metabolic data, starting with body composition information transmitted directly from a smart scale.

After logging this initial data in a dedicated app, Song prepares lemon water in an Owala bottle to accompany her medications. This beverage is also recorded in the application as part of the daily routine. The process marks a new rhythm in her daily life, centered on interacting with her digital counterpart.
summary: Victoria Song describes a 100-day routine where she feeds an AI digital twin her metabolic and body composition data. The system logs her health metrics and guides her dietary choices, such as drinking lemon water with medications.
author: The Verge

title: Anthropic warns small AI models could self-replicate through IoT devices
content: Anthropic has issued a warning that small AI models may possess the capability to self-replicate through Internet of Things (IoT) devices. The company noted that these "small weight-based replicators" could lead to the emergence of a new generation of computer worms.
summary: Anthropic warns that small AI models could self-replicate through IoT devices. The company notes that "Small weight-based replicators" could usher in a new generation of computer worms.
author: Ars Technica

title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 Day 2 Features AI Themes, Investor-Only Session, Roundtables
content:
Day 2 of TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 continued the event’s focus on emerging technology trends, featuring a full schedule of sessions that covered all themes across AI.  

The day also included an investor‑only session and additional roundtables, offering attendees deeper dives into specific topics.  

Participants are encouraged to register early to save 50 % on their pass.
summary: Day 2 of TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 covered a wide range of AI themes, included an investor-only session, and featured additional roundtables. Attendees can register now to receive a 50% discount on their pass.
author: TechCrunch

title: Netflix to cut 1,000 staff, targeting product, tech, legal, HR
content:
Netflix announced it will lay off 1,000 employees amid intensifying competition for user attention.
