The company said most of the cuts will affect its product, tech, legal, and human resources departments.  

The layoffs are part of a broader effort to adjust staffing levels.
summary: Netflix announced it will lay off 1,000 employees. Most of the cuts will affect its product, tech, legal, and human resources departments.
author: TechCrunch

title: Floqer Launches AI Agents to Research Sales Prospects, Eliminating Manual Effort
content:
Floqer has launched AI agents that research sales prospects, allowing teams to focus on other tasks.  

The company’s approach targets a challenge that is familiar to anyone who has worked in sales or revenue operations.  

Floqer’s solution is designed to streamline prospect research for sales teams.
summary: Floqer has introduced AI agents that research sales prospects so teams don’t have to. The company’s solution addresses a familiar problem for those in sales or revenue operations.
author: TechCrunch

title: Zenzap raises $44M to launch AI chat app targeting workplace WhatsApp replacement
content:
Zenzap has secured $44 million in funding for its AI‑powered chat application, which the company says is designed to replace WhatsApp in the workplace. The new capital will support the development and expansion of the platform’s features aimed at corporate communication.

The app is already in use by several notable organizations, including Starbucks and Taco Bell, according to the company’s announcement.
summary: Zenzap raised $44M to develop an AI chat app that seeks to replace WhatsApp in workplace settings. The platform is already used by organizations such as Starbucks and Taco Bell.
author: TechCrunch

title: Save 50% on your TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 ticket and join the last 2 days in San Francisco’s Moscone West
content:
TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 will take place in San Francisco on October 14‑15, with the event held at Moscone West.  

A promotion offers a 50 % discount on tickets for the last two days of the conference.  

Registrants are encouraged to sign up now to join the startup ecosystem and attend sessions focused on physical and software AI.
summary: Get a 50% discount on the last two days of TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, October 14-15, in San Francisco. Register now and join the rest of the startup ecosystem.
author: TechCrunch

title: Prismm lets account holders pre‑grant family access to accounts, keeping inherited money in‑house
content:
Prismm is a service designed to help banks retain inherited funds within their own institutions. By enabling account holders to grant designated family members pre‑approved access, the platform aims to keep money and related documents in‑house.

With Prismm, account holders can give those family members access to their accounts and documents ahead of time, allowing a smoother transition of assets when inheritance occurs. This approach is intended to maintain the flow of inherited money within the bank’s existing framework.
summary: With Prismm, account holders can give designated family members access to their accounts and documents ahead of time. The service is intended to help banks keep inherited money in-house.
author: TechCrunch

title: Mosqitter transforms mosquito traps into AI surveillance network
content:
Mosqitter is converting its existing mosquito-trapping hardware into an artificial intelligence-powered surveillance network. The system is designed to identify mosquito species and monitor their populations.

By leveraging this technology, Mosqitter aims to provide earlier warnings regarding the risks associated with mosquito-borne diseases.
summary: Mosqitter is converting its mosquito-trapping hardware into an AI-powered surveillance network. The system will identify species, monitor populations, and issue earlier warnings of mosquito-borne disease risks.
author: TechCrunch

title: Jason O'Connell suspected of using smart glasses as teleprompter in Senedd debate
content:
Jason O’Connell, the Senedd member for Pontypridd Cynon Merthyr, is suspected of using smart glasses as a teleprompter during a debate on 30 September. Video footage captured periodic flashing in his spectacles while he spoke for five minutes without looking at his notes.

In the days following the incident, other Welsh assembly members stated that the use of smart glasses, a technology popularized by Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta, required prompt attention. They called for the development of explicit guidance regarding the use of such devices in the assembly.

There is no suggestion that O’Connell's glasses were recording during the debate.
summary: Jason O’Connell, the Senedd member for Pontypridd Cynon Merthyr, is suspected of using smart glasses that displayed a teleprompter while speaking for five minutes on 30 September. Other Welsh assembly members have called for clear guidance on the use of such devices.
author: Guardian Technology

title: FBI Warns of AI-Enabled Terrorist Threats After Palm Springs Car Bomb
content:
In May 2025, a 25-year-old man detonated a car bomb outside a fertility clinic in Palm Springs, killing himself and injuring four others. While the attack highlighted threats to reproductive care facilities, the FBI identified it as evidence that bad actors are using generative AI to plan and execute terror plots. According to a previously unreported document reviewed by the Guardian, the suspect used an unnamed generative AI tool that failed to detect his request for bomb-making instructions. Law enforcement officers noted in the memo that the privacy of the suspect’s conversation with the AI chatbot hindered police from alerting authorities that someone was seeking instructions on how to make a bomb.

US law enforcement agencies, ranging from the FBI to local police departments, are increasingly warning about the dual threats of AI-enabled terrorism and anti-tech extremism. These warnings address how extremists could utilize AI to devise attacks, recruit new members, and disseminate content such as deepfakes, election misinformation, and child sexual abuse material. Authorities are also monitoring social media for opposition to AI and potential extremist attacks on datacenters.

The challenge for officers includes managing the use of AI tools for policing tasks, such as social media monitoring, while addressing public concern over these technologies. Additionally, law enforcement must navigate how individuals seeking information on weaponry or bombs can use AI to circumvent detection.
summary: In May 2025, a 25‑year‑old man detonated a car bomb outside a Palm Springs fertility clinic, killing himself and injuring four others. The FBI said the suspect used an unnamed generative AI tool to request bomb‑making instructions, and the privacy of the conversation prevented police from being alerted.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Palantir, Sadiq Khan drop legal battle over Met police contract
content:
Palantir and London Mayor Sadiq Khan have ended their legal dispute over a £50 million Metropolitan Police contract. The fight stemmed from claims that the mayor had blocked the U.S. tech firm from signing the deal because of concerns over its values and ethics.

On Wednesday, Palantir and the mayor’s Office of Policing and Crime (MOPAC) announced that they had withdrawn allegations against each other. The withdrawal averted a High Court trial that was scheduled for January.

The cancellation of the legal battle resolves the dispute between the tech company and the mayor’s office.
summary: Palantir and the London mayor's office of policing and crime (Mopac) announced they had withdrawn allegations against each other, ending the legal dispute. The dispute involved claims that the Labour mayor was blocking the US tech firm from signing a £50m Metropolitan police contract over concerns about its values and ethics.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Reform UK MP Jason O’Connell’s smart glasses spark ban calls in Westminster
content:
Jason O’Connell, a Reform UK member of the Senedd, was accused of using smart glasses to assist his five‑minute speech in the chamber.  Observers noted periodic flashing in the spectacles, suggesting the device was providing prompts while O’Connell spoke without looking at his notes.  

During the address he cited data from Cardiff, noting that 192 roads had been reviewed following 933 requests, yet only four routes had been returned to 30‑mph limits.  He also argued that the 20‑mph traffic zone policy had cost £38.3 million to implement and could lead to up to £8.9 billion in economic self‑harm.
summary: Jason O’Connell, a Reform UK Senedd member, used AI‑enabled smart glasses during a five‑minute speech in the Senedd chamber, which prompted calls for a ban in Westminster. In his speech, he criticized the 20mph traffic zones, citing that only four routes returned to 30mph after reviewing 192 roads and 933 requests, and claimed £38.3m was wasted on the policy and up to £8.9bn in economic self‑harm.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Kazakhstan seeks Belgium partnership for Middle Corridor trade
content:
Kazakhstan is seeking closer cooperation with Belgium on the Middle Corridor, a development announced as King Philippe and Queen Mathilde make their first state visit to the country.

The Kazakh government is exploring a potential partnership between the Port of Antwerp‑Bruges and the Caspian ports of Aktau and Kuryk.

The visit marks the first state visit of King Philippe and Queen Mathilde to Kazakhstan.
summary: Kazakhstan is seeking closer cooperation with Belgium on the Middle Corridor, including a potential partnership between the Port of Antwerp-Bruges and the Caspian ports of Aktau and Kuryk. The talks come as King Philippe and Queen Mathilde make their first state visit to the country.
author: Euronews

title: Supporters Rally in Hamburg as Trial Opens Over Nord Stream Pipeline Blasts
content:
Supporters waving Ukrainian flags gathered outside a court in Hamburg on Wednesday, 14 October, in solidarity with a former Ukrainian army officer accused of involvement in the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline explosions in the Baltic Sea.  

The gathering came as the trial opens over the Nord Stream pipeline blasts.
summary: Supporters waving Ukrainian flags gathered outside a Hamburg court on Wednesday, 14 October. They were in solidarity with a former Ukrainian army officer accused of involvement in the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline explosions in the Baltic Sea.
author: Euronews

title: Russia’s Internet Shutdowns Drive State Firms Back to Landline Phones
content:
Russia’s internet shutdowns push state firms back to landline phones

State procurement of landline telephones tripled in the first eight months of 2026 as mobile internet outages hit nearly 80% of the country. The surge in demand reflects widespread disruptions that have forced many organizations to rely on traditional telephone lines for communication.

Rostelecom’s chief urged Russians to keep a landline at home “like a fire extinguisher,” emphasizing the importance of maintaining a reliable contact method amid the ongoing connectivity challenges.
summary: State procurement of landline telephones tripled in the first eight months of 2026 as mobile internet outages hit nearly 80% of the country. Rostelecom’s chief urged Russians to keep one at home like a fire extinguisher.
author: Euronews

title: One killed, 20 injured in overnight Russian attacks on Kyiv
content:
One person was killed and 20 others injured during overnight Russian attacks on Kyiv, according to Ukrainian authorities.  

The authorities say that some of the strikes targeted energy infrastructure.  

The attacks occurred a few days after US President Donald Trump announced an “energy ceasefire.”
summary: Ukrainian authorities report that one person was killed and 20 others injured in overnight Russian attacks on Kyiv, with some strikes targeting energy infrastructure. These attacks occurred a few days after US President Donald Trump announced an 'energy ceasefire'.
author: Euronews

title: Ukraine seeks clarification from US, SpaceX, NATO on Starlink access limits
content:
Ukraine is contacting the United States, SpaceX and NATO to seek clarification on limitations imposed on its use of the Starlink satellite‑internet system. A source from Ukraine’s Defence Ministry said the request was made on Wednesday.

Ukrainian troops have reported that the Starlink connection is being shut off when travelling at higher speeds, causing major disruption to drone operations. Many of the drones depend on satellite internet to pilot the craft.
summary: Ukraine's Defence Ministry says it is contacting the United States, SpaceX and NATO to clarify limits on its use of the Starlink satellite internet system. Ukrainian troops report that the Starlink connection shuts off at higher speeds, disrupting drone operations that rely on the service.
author: France 24

title: France High Schools Remain Closed Amid Rising Student Protests
content:
Some high schools in France remained closed on Wednesday, a day after tens of thousands of people joined rallies across the country to support protesting students.  

The closures followed a wave of demonstrations that saw students and supporters rallying nationwide.  

On Saturday, national demonstrations against the spiralling cost of living are scheduled to take place, with unions and student groups reporting that the two protest currents are fusing together.
summary: Some high schools in France remained closed on Wednesday after tens of thousands joined rallies supporting protesting students. National demonstrations against the spiralling cost of living are scheduled for Saturday, with unions and student groups fusing together.
author: France 24

title: Cornell bans fraternity house parties through academic year after alleged gang rape
content:
Cornell University announced on Tuesday that it will ban parties and social events at fraternity houses through the end of the academic year, according to President Michael Kotlikoff. The action follows an outcry over an alleged gang rape on campus in 2024 and a lawsuit filed by former undergraduate Jane Doe, who alleges seven men sexually assaulted her during a party.

The university’s leadership has faced heavy criticism in recent weeks over its response to the allegations. The ban on fraternity house gatherings will remain in effect until the academic year concludes.
summary: Cornell University will ban parties and social events at fraternity houses until the end of the academic year, its president Michael Kotlikoff said on Tuesday. The ban follows criticism and a lawsuit by former undergraduate Jane Doe alleging seven men sexually assaulted her during a party in an alleged 2024 campus gang rape.
author: France 24

title: Ukraine says SpaceX limited Starlink, crippling drones amid worsening US ties
content:
Kyiv accused Elon Musk’s SpaceX on Wednesday of restricting Starlink services, saying the limitation has crippled Ukrainian drones.  

The allegation came as Russian missile strikes knocked out power stations, attacks that President Volodymyr Zelensky described as “ostentatious disrespect” to Donald Trump. Kyiv’s relationship with Washington has deteriorated since U.S. President Trump abruptly lifted sanctions on Russian diesel last week and publicly turned on Zelensky.  

The report was filed by FRANCE 24’s Gulliver Cragg from Kyiv.
summary: Ukraine accused Elon Musk's SpaceX on Wednesday of limiting Starlink service, saying it crippled its drones. The claim follows Russian missile strikes that knocked out power stations and a sharp deterioration in Kyiv's ties with Washington after President Trump lifted sanctions on Russian diesel and publicly turned on Zelensky.
author: France 24

title: King Felipe VI says Ceuta and Melilla inalienable during key visit
content:
King Felipe VI said on Tuesday that Ceuta and Melilla are “an inalienable part” of Spain while making a landmark visit to the North African territories claimed by neighboring Morocco.  

The monarch, who rarely makes political statements, stressed the need for Spain to “maintain good neighbourly relations” with Rabat after an unprecedented migrant surge into Ceuta in July strained historically delicate ties.  

The remarks were reported by FRANCE 24’s Sarah Morris from Madrid.
summary: King Felipe VI said Ceuta and Melilla were an inalienable part of Spain during a landmark visit to the north African territories claimed by Morocco. He emphasized Spain's need to maintain good neighbourly relations with Rabat after July's unprecedented migrant surge into Ceuta strained historically delicate ties.
author: France 24

title: Houthis claim attack on Saudi Aramco facilities and say more strikes will follow
content:
Yemen’s Iran‑backed Houthis said on Wednesday that they had targeted facilities belonging to Saudi oil giant Saudi Aramco. The claim followed Saudi officials’ report of a strike on a building in an area that houses the energy company’s operations centre.

Powerful explosions rattled the Saudi capital, Riyadh, as the coalition fighting the Houthis announced it had intercepted a missile fired by the group toward the city.

The Houthis said the attack was part of a broader campaign and vowed to carry out more attacks.
summary: Yemen's Houthis said they had targeted facilities belonging to Saudi Aramco after Saudi officials reported a strike on a building in an area housing the energy giant's operations centre. Powerful explosions rattled the Saudi capital, and the coalition fighting the Houthis said it intercepted a missile fired by the Iran‑backed group toward Riyadh.
author: France 24

title: Phoenix youth activists of Turning Point USA rally to honor Charlie Kirk ahead of midterms
content:
Young ultra‑conservatives in Phoenix are mobilizing to preserve the legacy of far‑right influencer Charlie Kirk, who was assassinated in September 2025. The activists, members of Turning Point USA—the organization Kirk co‑founded—are focusing their efforts on energizing the youth electorate ahead of the upcoming U.S. midterm elections.

More than a year after Kirk’s death, the group says it is working “tirelessly” to honor his memory by organizing rallies, canvassing, and voter‑registration drives aimed at young voters. Their goal is to translate Kirk’s influence into electoral support for conservative candidates in the forthcoming midterms.
summary: More than a year after the September 2025 assassination of far‑right influencer Charlie Kirk, young activists from Turning Point USA are active in Phoenix. They are working to honour his legacy by rallying the youth vote ahead of the US midterm elections.
author: France 24

title: Houthis say they hit Aramco facilities and threaten more Saudi attacks
content:
Yemen's Houthi rebels announced on Wednesday that they had targeted facilities belonging to Saudi oil giant Aramco following a strike reported by officials in Riyadh on a building located in the area that houses the energy company's headquarters.

The Iran‑backed militia also claimed to have launched missile strikes on the Saudi capital, Riyadh, and said the attacks were part of a broader campaign against the kingdom.

The Houthis vowed to continue striking Saudi airports and oil facilities, indicating an intent to further escalate their operations.
summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels said they had targeted facilities belonging to Saudi oil giant Aramco after Riyadh officials reported a strike on a building in the area housing the company's headquarters. The Iran-back militia also claimed missile strikes on Riyadh and vowed to continue attacking Saudi airports and oil facilities.
author: France 24

title: Fact check: Viral graph on Russian data‑center attacks and AfD bot activity is misleading
content:
A fact‑check has examined a viral graph that suggested attacks on Russian data centers led to a decline in bot activity surrounding Germany’s Alternative for Germany (AfD) party. The graphic was widely shared as evidence of a causal link between the cyber‑attacks and reduced online manipulation.

The review found the graph to contain significant inconsistencies and noted that it offers no supporting evidence for the claimed reduction in bot activity. Consequently, the claim that the attacks diminished Russian‑linked bot operations around the AfD is unsubstantiated.
summary: A viral graph claimed that attacks on Russian data centers reduced bot activity around Germany's AfD. The fact check found significant inconsistencies in the graph and no evidence supporting the claim.
author: DW World

title: Climate change and drone attacks worsen Sudan's humanitarian crisis, health system at risk
content:
Climate change and drone attacks are worsening an already severe humanitarian crisis in war‑torn Sudan, according to the headline.

Aid groups have warned that the country’s health system faces an imminent collapse as fighting continues to displace civilians during the planting season.

The United Nations has responded by extending an arms embargo, but the measure applies only to the Darfur region.
summary: Aid groups say the health system in Sudan could collapse as fighting displaces civilians during the planting season. The United Nations has extended an arms embargo limited to Darfur.
author: DW World

title: Riot police deployed in Tirana as students protest after fire at Education Ministry
content:
A fire broke out at Albania’s Education Ministry in the capital Tirana as students staged protests, according to reports.

Riot police were deployed in Tirana on the second day of the demonstrations, and the sudden outbreak was noted as reminiscent of the widespread protests in France that have attracted international attention.
summary: Riot police were deployed in Tirana on the second day of student protests. The protests, sparked by a fire at the Education Ministry, were compared to recent demonstrations in France.
author: DW World

title: India urges Russia and Ukraine to ensure safe Black Sea commercial shipping
content: New Delhi has called on both Moscow and Kyiv to guarantee the safety of commercial vessels operating in the Black Sea. The Indian government said the request comes as recent attacks in the region have placed Indian seafarers at risk.
summary: New Delhi wants Moscow and Kyiv to ensure safe commercial shipping in the Black Sea. The request comes amid attacks that put Indian seafarers at risk.
author: DW World

title: WHO urges urgent health action in Eastern Mediterranean
content:
The head of the World Health Organization has urged immediate action to promote, provide and protect health across the Eastern Mediterranean region. The call comes as the area faces some of the world’s most severe humanitarian crises.

The WHO chief highlighted Sudan, Yemen and the Occupied Palestinian Territory as key locations where urgent health measures are needed.
summary: The head of the World Health Organization called for promoting, providing and protecting health in the Eastern Mediterranean region. The region includes major humanitarian crises such as Sudan, Yemen and the Occupied Palestinian Territory.
author: UN News

title: WFP warns humanitarian catastrophe in Yemen as fighting blocks aid to 800,000
content:
The United Nations World Food Programme warned on Wednesday that intensifying fighting in Yemen could trigger a humanitarian catastrophe as aid deliveries are increasingly blocked.  

The agency said the conflict has cut off life‑saving assistance for 800,000 people, with shifting frontlines, blocked roads and growing insecurity severely restricting access to the city of Taiz and other conflict zones.
summary: The UN World Food Programme said intensifying fighting in Yemen has cut off life‑saving assistance to 800,000 people. Shifting frontlines, blocked roads and growing insecurity have severely restricted access to Taiz and other conflict zones.
author: UN News

title: Guinea-Bissau health minister denies approval of Danish hepatitis B newborn trial
content:
Guinea‑Bissau’s health minister said on Tuesday that the government has not authorized a Danish‑led hepatitis B trial in newborns, refuting claims that the country approved the controversial study.

The proposed research, which would be funded by the United States government and private partners, has been promoted by Robert F. Kennedy Jr., identified in the report as the secretary of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services and a longtime anti‑vaccine activist.

According to the minister, the trial would not examine vaccine safety or effectiveness; instead it would monitor “nonspecific” health outcomes such as overall mortality and neurodevelopmental conditions.
summary: Guinea-Bissau's health minister said the government did not authorize the Danish-led hepatitis B trial in newborns. The study, funded by the US government and private partners, would track nonspecific health outcomes such as overall mortality and neurodevelopmental conditions rather than vaccine safety or effectiveness.
author: Guardian World

title: Three Saudi Pro League matches postponed after Houthi attacks, including Al Nassr
content:
The Saudi Pro League announced the postponement of three matches after Houthi attacks, one of which involves Al Nassr, the club of Cristiano Ronaldo.  

The league’s decision affects the scheduled fixtures for the three affected teams, with Al Nassr’s game among those delayed.
summary: The Saudi Pro League postponed three games following Houthi attacks. One of the delayed matches involves Cristiano Ronaldo's Al Nassr side.
author: Al Jazeera

title: UN urges Israel to increase actions against settler violence
content:
The United Nations has called on Israel to take additional measures to stop settler violence, according to a report in Jerusalem Daily.  

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned again that Israel’s “enemies” are planning an attack before the upcoming elections.  

Both the UN demand and Netanyahu’s warning were highlighted in the Jerusalem Daily article.
summary: The UN has demanded that Israel do more to stop settler violence. Netanyahu warned again that Israel’s ‘enemies’ are planning an attack before elections.
author: Al Jazeera

title: UN official warns food crisis if Hormuz fertiliser plan stalls
content:
A United Nations official warned that a looming food crisis could arise as the plan to move fertiliser through the Hormuz Strait stalls.  

The official said that without a quick deal to transport fertiliser through the strait, agricultural productivity would “significantly drop.”
summary: A UN official warned that a stalled fertiliser plan through the Hormuz Strait could lead to a looming food crisis. The official said agricultural productivity would "significantly drop" without a quick deal to move fertiliser through the strait.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US Social Security benefits to increase 3.6% in 2027
content:
US Social Security benefits are set to rise by 3.6 percent in 2027, according to the announcement.  

The increase will add roughly $75 to the monthly checks received by retired Americans, a boost that comes as many face widespread inflation challenges.
summary: Benefits will rise by 3.6 percent in 2027. Retired Americans will receive about $75 more per month.
author: Al Jazeera

title: At least two security officials killed near Iran's critical Chabahar port
content:
At least two security officials were killed in an incident near Iran’s strategic Chabahar port, according to Iranian authorities.  

Iran said the attack was carried out by “terrorist groups” that receive support from outside the country and are targeting the nation’s security forces.
summary: At least two security officials were killed near Iran's critical Chabahar port. Iran says 'terrorist groups' supported from outside the country are targeting security forces.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Tehran municipality accused of overstep after launching welfare projects
content:
Tehran’s municipal government has launched a series of new welfare projects, prompting accusations that the initiative represents an “overstep” by the city’s authorities.  

Critics have focused on the projects’ funding sources, questioned their transparency, and raised concerns that they may contribute to inflation.
summary: The Tehran municipality has been accused of overstepping after launching new welfare projects. The projects have faced intense criticism over funding sources, transparency and inflation claims.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Albania experiments with artificial intelligence in politics
content:
Albania is experimenting with artificial intelligence in politics, a development highlighted in a recent analysis titled “AI in politics: Is Albania the EU’s testing ground?”  

The country's foray into AI-driven political applications marks a notable shift toward integrating advanced technology within its governance framework.  

The article’s title raises the question of whether Albania is being used as a testing ground for the European Union’s broader AI initiatives.
summary: Albania is experimenting with artificial intelligence in politics. The experiment focuses on political applications.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Saudi OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan arrested by FBI after more than a year at company
content:
A Saudi engineer at OpenAI, Abdulrahman Alfozan, was taken into custody by the FBI, a case that has been described in reports with references to “toilet paper and secret recorders.”  

Alfozan had been employed by the AI company for more than a year before the arrest. The FBI’s action marks the latest development in the investigation of the OpenAI employee.
summary: Abdulrahman Alfozan, a Saudi engineer, worked for OpenAI for more than a year. He was arrested by the FBI.
author: BBC World

title: Australia’s first Michelin stars awarded to 11 South Australian restaurants
content:
Australia’s inaugural Michelin stars have been awarded to 11 restaurants, all located in South Australia.  

The concentration of the awards in a single state follows reports that the South Australian government financed incognito inspectors to assess the venues.  

These 11 establishments thus become the first Australian restaurants to receive Michelin recognition.
summary: Australia’s first-ever Michelin stars were awarded to 11 restaurants. All of the restaurants are in South Australia, reportedly because the state government paid for incognito inspectors to visit.
author: BBC World

title: US inflation climbs to 3.7% in year to September, driven by motor fuel costs
content: U.S. inflation accelerated to an annual rate of 3.7% for the year ending in September, outpacing expectations. The increase was largely driven by higher motor fuel costs, which lifted overall price growth. The rise signals a broader upward pressure on consumer prices across the United States.
summary: The pace of price rises increased to 3.7% in the year to September. The increase was driven by higher motor fuel costs.
author: BBC World

title: Selma Blair charged with two counts of assault after plane incident
content: Selma Blair, known for her role in Legally Blonde, is facing two counts of assault following an incident on a flight. The charges stem from allegations that she kicked a police officer and a nurse after previously attacking flight attendants during the journey.
summary: The Legally Blonde actress faces two counts of assault for allegedly kicking a police officer and a nurse. These charges follow an alleged attack on attendants during a flight.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Russell T Davies criticises BBC boss's 'clumsy' AI Doctor Who comments
content: BBC director general Matt Brittin has drawn criticism from Russell T Davies after stating he had watched a "pretty good" AI-generated episode of Doctor Who. Davies described Brittin’s remarks on the use of artificial intelligence in the production of the series as "clumsy."
summary: BBC director general Matt Brittin said he had seen a "pretty good" AI-generated episode of Doctor Who. Russell T Davies criticised the director general's comments as clumsy.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Davina McCall says post‑brain surgery memory loss felt like advanced Alzheimer’s
content:
Davina McCall has said that the memory loss she experienced after brain surgery felt like “advanced Alzheimer’s.”  

The TV presenter revealed that she underwent an operation to remove a benign tumour.  

She reported that following the procedure she suffered memory loss.
summary: TV presenter Davina McCall said she suffered memory loss after an operation to remove a benign tumour. She described the loss as feeling like advanced Alzheimer’s.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Shakhtar Donetsk sets up London base for Champions League away from Ukraine
content:
Shakhtar Donetsk, managed by Arda Turan, are based in London for their Champions League campaign, with Chelsea’s Stamford Bridge set to host their home matches as the club lacks a home ground in Ukraine. The team’s statement, “We’re here to show the world that we are alive,” underscores their determination to continue competing despite the ongoing conflict.

In a separate report from their temporary base in Ukraine, the club maintains a spa hotel facility 15 minutes outside Lviv. During a training session, manager Arda Turan and director of football Darijo Srna were observed interacting with players, with Srna demonstrating a skillful shot that prompted Turan to exclaim, “Modric!” This light training was reserved for players who did not start the previous day’s match against Veres Rivne.

The presence of the team in Ukraine remains subject to security risks, as air raid sirens disrupted their peace around dawn at the Lviv base. Similarly, during the match in Rivne, located three hours to the north-east, an alarm forced players and staff into a stadium shelter, delaying the second half by 20 minutes.
summary: Shakhtar Donetsk has established a base in London to host their Champions League matches, with Chelsea's Stamford Bridge serving as their venue. The team continues to face security threats from Russian attacks while training in Ukraine, where air raid sirens regularly disrupt their daily routines.
author: Guardian Sport

title: David Silva to end retirement for one match with Hong Kong club Supreme Sha Tin
content:
Former Manchester City midfielder David Silva is set to make a brief return to professional football at the age of 40, agreeing to play a single match for Supreme Sha Tin. The former international will join a roster of notable players who have previously competed in the territory, including George Best, Bobby Moore, and Diego Forlán.

Hong Kong’s local Premier League has recently sought to elevate its profile, following years of attempts to maintain an independent football association while navigating its status as a special administrative region of China. Although efforts to place a local team in the Chinese Super League during a period of high spending did not materialize, the local league has continued to attract high-profile talent.

Silva’s appearance marks the latest addition to a long history of football in the city, which began during its time as a British colony and has persisted since 1997. The match offers the ambitious club a one-day opportunity to feature a former Premier League star on their team.
summary: Former Manchester City midfielder David Silva is coming out of retirement at age 40 to play a single match for the Hong Kong club Supreme Sha Tin. The article notes that Silva will join a long list of former international stars who have played in the territory.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Sunderland to face Torreense in Portugal after 53 years away from Europe
content:
Sunderland prepares to travel to Portugal on Thursday night to face Torreense in the Europa League, marking the club’s first competitive appearance on European soil in 53 years. The visit offers a symbolic parallel to the Black Cats’ last European outing, which was a second leg of a European Cup Winners’ Cup tie against Sporting in Lisbon. That previous encounter occurred when Sunderland were FA Cup holders competing in the Second Division.

Torreense, also a second-tier side, has generated surprise by securing a spot in the Europa League’s initial phase after defeating Sporting in the Portuguese Cup final last season. The Portuguese club’s campaign was further strengthened last month when they recorded a 2-1 victory over Lillestrom in Norway, boosting their prospects for advancing to next spring’s sudden-death rounds. This match provides Sunderland with a respite from a difficult start to their Premier League season.
summary: Sunderland will play Torreense in the Europa League, marking the club's first competitive European match in 53 years. The Black Cats are using this trip as a break from their difficult start to the Premier League season.
author: Guardian Sport

title: New biography details Renée Richards' 1977 US Open lawsuit and current stance
content:
In 1977, ophthalmologist Dr. Renée Richards sued for the right to compete in the women’s draw of the US Open following a sex-change operation. At the time, Richards had excelled as a male amateur player, and her legal battle dominated tennis headlines. The case was successfully argued by the firm of Roy Cohn, who is better known for prosecuting suspected communists during the red scare and mentoring Donald Trump.

A new biography titled Finding Renée Richards: The Groundbreaking Story of Tennis’s Trans Pioneer by Julie Kliegman explores this complex legacy. The book details the narrative of Richards’s 1977 lawsuit and highlights her current stance, as she now supports bans on trans athletes in women’s sports.
summary: A new biography by Julie Kliegman explores the complex legacy of tennis pioneer Renée Richards. The book covers her 1977 lawsuit to play in the US Open, where she was represented by Roy Cohn, and notes her current support for bans on trans athletes in women's sports.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England winger Feyi-Waboso on track for Nations Championship after hamstring tweak
content:
England’s game-breaking winger Manny Feyi-Waboso is on track to be fit for international duty next month, despite tweaking a hamstring during Exeter’s match against Newcastle on Sunday. title: Nonprofit Opens Free 3D Digital Leonardo da Vinci Museum
content:
The founder of a small nonprofit has launched Museum of Ages, a digital Leonardo da Vinci museum featuring a virtual tour with 17 stops. The free entrance includes close-to-real-size views of his paintings, 15 machines rebuilt in code, and 29 anatomy sheets. Visitors can also examine 207 selected manuscript pages in a virtual reading table, with 131 of those pages translated, and explore a reconstruction of da Vinci’s last house in Amboise.

The museum is available in seven languages and labels each stop with one of four grades: documented, reconstructed, conjectural, or not known. Detailed views allow users to inspect the sources for each element. The project utilizes Three.js for materials and runs on WebGPU, with WebGL2 as a fallback for unsupported browsers. Textures are derived from Creative Commons Zero photo scans and free 3D models.

The organization’s mission is to create walkable digital museums for individuals unable to visit physical locations due to illness, disability, cost, or distance. To ensure accessibility, the walk was pre-rendered to function on older phones and accommodate older users. The code is released under the AGPL-3.0 license, while texts and pictures are licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0.
summary: The nonprofit Museum of Ages released a free virtual tour featuring 17 stops, including 15 rebuilt machines and 207 manuscript pages. The project uses WebGPU and Three.js to make museums accessible to people with disabilities or financial constraints.
