The man in the real footage, identified by the BBC as William Chapman, later died from his injuries following the Saturday incident, police said.
summary: Trump faced backlash after posting a video that showed a UK man being killed by a tiger. Police said the man, identified by the BBC as William Chapman, later died from his injuries following the Saturday incident.
author: Euronews

title: Duane Davis sentenced to minimum 40 years for orchestrating Tupac Shakur's murder
content:
Duane Davis has been sentenced to a minimum of 40 years in prison for orchestrating the murder of Tupac Shakur.  

Shakur was a key figure in a hip‑hop rivalry pitting the US East Coast against the West Coast. He was just 25 when he was gunned down in Las Vegas.
summary: Duane Davis was sentenced to a minimum of 40 years in prison for orchestrating the murder of Tupac Shakur. Shakur, a 25‑year‑old key figure in the East Coast–West Coast hip‑hop rivalry, was gunned down in Las Vegas.
author: Euronews

title: Iran executes Ali‑Sina Mostafavi, accused of armed attacks during US‑Israeli strikes
content:
Iran has executed Ali‑Sina Mostafavi, a 38‑year‑old mountaineer and musician from Kerman, on charges of “enmity against God.”  

Mostafavi was accused of firing on civilians and soldiers during the opening months of the war.  He was also charged with participating in the January protests and sending footage.
summary: Ali‑Sina Mostafavi, a 38‑year‑old mountaineer and musician from Kerman, was executed in Iran on charges of “enmity against God.” He was accused of firing on civilians and soldiers during the opening months of the war, and of participating in the January protests and sending footage.
author: Euronews

title: Midday news bulletin for October 14 2026 covering Europe and global stories
content:
On October 14th, 2026, the midday news bulletin offers a concise update on the most important stories from around Europe and beyond. The bulletin highlights the latest news and breaking news across a range of topics.

The coverage includes world events, business developments, entertainment releases, political updates, cultural highlights, and travel news.
summary: The bulletin invites readers to catch up on the most important stories from Europe and beyond on October 14 2026. It includes coverage of world, business, entertainment, politics, culture and travel.
author: Euronews

title: King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia visit Ceuta in first royal trip since 2007
content:
King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia arrived in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta on Tuesday, where cheering crowds waved Spanish flags as the royal couple made a diplomatically sensitive visit.  

The trip follows a surge of migrants from Morocco that entered Ceuta in July, and it marks the first time the monarchs have visited the city since 2007, when a diplomatic crisis erupted with neighbouring Morocco. Morocco claims sovereignty over Ceuta and Spain’s other North African territory, Melilla.  

The visit highlights Spain’s reaffirmation of its authority over the enclave.
summary: King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia arrived in Ceuta on Tuesday amid cheering crowds waving Spanish flags. The visit, the first by Spanish royals since 2007, came after a July migrant influx from Morocco and occurs despite Morocco’s claim of sovereignty over Ceuta and Melilla.
author: France 24

title: Ukrainian ex-military officer Serhii K. on trial in Germany for Nord Stream sabotage
content:
A Ukrainian ex‑military officer began a trial in Germany on Wednesday, charged with organising the covert operation that destroyed the Nord Stream gas pipelines in September 2022, cutting western Europe off from Russia’s largest natural‑gas source.  

The suspect, identified under German privacy rules only as Serhii K., is alleged to have led a team of Ukrainian agents that included divers and an explosives expert to carry out what officials describe as one of the biggest infrastructure sabotage operations of modern times.  

FRANCE 24’s Jörg Taszman reported the proceedings from Berlin.  

The case is being heard before a German court.
summary: A Ukrainian ex-military officer identified as Serhii K. is on trial in Germany on Wednesday for allegedly organising the operation that blew up the Nord Stream gas pipelines in September 2022. He is accused of leading a group of Ukrainian agents, including divers and an explosives expert, in the sabotage.
author: France 24

title: Winnie the Pooh celebrates 100th anniversary
content:
Winnie the Pooh, the world’s most famous and very greedy bear, is celebrating his centenary this year.

The character made his debut in a story titled “The Wrong Kind of Bees” that appeared in the London Evening News. The first collection of Pooh stories, illustrated by E. H. Shepard, was published as a book on October 14, 1926.
summary: Winnie the Pooh is marking his centenary this year. He first appeared in the story “The Wrong Kind of Bees” in the London Evening News, and the initial collection illustrated by E. H. Shepard was published on October 14, 1926.
author: France 24

title: Scientists suggest some Super-Earths could be more habitable than Earth
content:
Scientists note that there may be planets more habitable than Earth elsewhere in the galaxy, raising the prospect that some Super‑Earths could offer conditions superior to those on our planet.  

The possibility of such worlds has prompted questions about whether they could ever be reached, though no specific missions or timelines were mentioned.  

The discussion appears alongside other international news items, but the scientific observation remains that more habitable planets might exist beyond Earth.
summary: Science news reports that there might be planets more habitable than Earth. The piece appears in a press review that also covers Portuguese housing, a German robot assault, and a Cosmopolitan dating article.
author: France 24

title: Rwanda to host Africa's first F1 Grand Prix in early 2030s under decade-long deal
content:
Rwanda and Formula One announced on Tuesday that the East African nation will host Africa’s first Formula One Grand Prix since 1993, slated for the early 2030s. The agreement is a decade‑long deal between the circuit and Rwanda.

The plan follows years of Rwanda’s efforts to use sports such as football and basketball to boost its image and attract investment, and it would mark the continent’s return to the F1 calendar after a three‑decade hiatus.

Human rights group Amnesty International criticised the arrangement, accusing Formula One of offering Rwanda a “sportswashing prize.”
summary: Rwanda will host Africa's first Formula One Grand Prix since 1993 in the early 2030s after a decade-long deal was announced on Tuesday. Amnesty International accused Formula One of offering Rwanda a sportswashing prize.
author: France 24

title: Dangote refinery extends IPO as plant reshapes Nigeria's fuel market
content:
The initial public offering for the Dangote Refinery was extended by two weeks and will now close on October 27, 2026, after a “huge popular success,” according to FRANCE 24’s Chinwe Ossundu.  

The extension comes as the escalation of conflict in the Middle East and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz have driven up global crude prices and created supply shortages, prompting African and European countries to turn in mass to the refinery.  

The plant, operated by the leading African producer of crude oil, aims to transform its role into a regional hub for refining and petrochemicals.
summary: The Dangote refinery's IPO was extended for two weeks and will close on October 27, 2026 after a huge popular response. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz and rising crude prices have prompted African and European countries to turn to the refinery, which seeks to become a regional hub for refining and petrochemicals.
author: France 24

title: World leaders and Vatican cardinals pray for Pope Leo after lung cancer diagnosis
content:
World leaders, Catholics worldwide and senior cardinals at the Vatican gathered to pray for Pope Leo on Wednesday after doctors announced that the 71‑year‑old pontiff had been diagnosed with lung cancer and had part of one lung removed.

The diagnosis, which shocked many, comes less than a year after Pope Leo’s election in May 2025, a period during which he was noted for his relative youth and energetic demeanor.
summary: World leaders, Catholics worldwide and senior Vatican cardinals offered prayers for Pope Leo on Wednesday after doctors announced the 71‑year‑old pontiff was diagnosed with lung cancer and had part of one lung removed. The pope, elected in May 2025 and described as relatively young and energetic, caused shock with the diagnosis.
author: France 24

title: Republicans pour hundreds of millions into defending red-state seats ahead of midterms
content:
U.S. President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that Republicans face an equally difficult fight to retain control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate in November’s midterm elections, even as forecasts suggest a considerably tougher contest for the House.

Despite the outlook, the party is allocating hundreds of millions of dollars to defend congressional and state‑level seats that were once considered safely red. In states such as North Carolina and Georgia, Republicans appear to be scaling back their ambitions, shifting resources to other Republican strongholds where Democrats are mounting unexpected challenges, according to France 24 International Affairs commentator Douglas Herbert.
summary: US President Donald Trump said Republicans face an equally difficult fight to retain control of both the House and Senate in the November midterm elections, despite forecasts of a tougher House contest. The party is spending hundreds of millions of dollars to defend previously safe red congressional and state seats, while scaling back in North Carolina and Georgia to shift resources to other Republican strongholds where Democrats pose unexpected challenges.
author: France 24

title: Former DRC President Joseph Kabila joins political‑military front with Rwandan‑backed M23
content:
Former Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) President Joseph Kabila has joined a new political‑military front that brings together the Rwandan‑backed AFC/M23 coalition, a move that raises questions over peace in the country.

The front unites the AFC/M23 coalition, known to receive support from Rwanda, with Kabila’s participation indicating a shift in alliances. Observers note that this alignment could affect ongoing efforts to stabilize the DRC.
summary: Former DRC President Joseph Kabila has joined a new political‑military front. The front brings together the Rwandan‑backed AFC/M23 coalition.
author: DW World

title: Hardliners pressure Iran government, demand removal of Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi
content:
Iran’s political landscape is becoming increasingly fraught as hardliners intensify pressure on the government. The current climate of infighting is highlighted by calls for the removal of Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi.

In addition to the push for Araghchi’s dismissal, the oil minister has resigned. Despite this leadership change, the pressure on President Masoud Pezeshkian has not eased.
summary: Hardliners are stepping up pressure on Iran's government and calling for Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi's removal. The oil minister resigned, but the move has done little to ease pressure on President Masoud Pezeshkian.
author: DW World

title: Trump announces new Super Intelligence taskforce with AI czar Jay Clayton
content: Trump announced a new Super Intelligence taskforce aimed at ensuring the United States maintains a leadership position in artificial intelligence development. The initiative is overseen by White House AI czar Jay Clayton, who will direct a group focused on advancing U.S. competitiveness in AI on the global stage. The announcement signals a renewed emphasis on national investment and coordination in the field of artificial intelligence.
summary: Trump announced a new Super Intelligence taskforce. The taskforce is led by White House AI czar Jay Clayton and is responsible for ensuring the US leads international competition in artificial intelligence development.
author: DW World

title: General Assembly adopts pandemic prevention declaration with 153 votes, three against
content:
The United Nations General Assembly adopted a political declaration on pandemic prevention, preparedness and response on Monday. The resolution passed with 153 votes in favour, three votes against, and two abstentions.

The three countries that voted against the declaration were Argentina, Israel and the United States. New Zealand and Paraguay abstained from voting.
summary: The General Assembly on Monday adopted a political declaration on pandemic prevention, preparedness and response. The vote was 153 in favour, three against (Argentina, Israel and United States) and two abstentions (New Zealand and Paraguay).
author: UN News

title: UN Special Representative urges stronger global action to protect children in crises
content:
The UN Special Representative on Violence Against Children warned that global action to end violence against children is lagging behind the growing risks faced by boys and girls in crises. The representative called for stronger worldwide efforts to protect children caught up in an increasing number of emergencies.

According to the statement, current measures are insufficient, leaving many children vulnerable to violence as crises multiply. The UN expert urged the international community to intensify its response to safeguard children worldwide.
summary: The UN Special Representative on Violence Against Children said current global efforts to protect children are insufficient. He called for stronger action to safeguard boys and girls affected by an increasing number of crises.
author: UN News

title: Disasters cause $228 billion in annual housing losses worldwide
content:
Disasters cost $228 billion in housing losses every year, a figure that highlights the financial burden communities around the world face when rebuilding after a disaster strikes.  

The $228 billion represents the amount of money communities must find annually to replace damaged or destroyed homes. This figure underscores the scale of the challenge in restoring housing following natural or man‑made disasters.
summary: Communities around the world face $228 billion in housing losses each year. The figure represents the cost of rebuilding homes after disasters strike.
author: UN News

title: Russian attacks kill residents and injure dozens in Kharkiv and Kyiv
content: Russian attacks on Ukraine’s two largest cities, Kharkiv and Kyiv, have again killed and injured civilians, damaging homes and civilian infrastructure, the UN aid coordination office (OCHA) said on Tuesday. The attacks occurred in recent days, according to the OCHA statement.
summary: Russian attacks on Ukraine’s two largest cities, Kharkiv and Kyiv, have killed residents and injured dozens of civilians. The attacks also damaged homes and civilian infrastructure, the UN aid coordination office (OCHA) said on Tuesday.
author: UN News

title: UN chief says need for UN never greater, proposes $3.3 billion budget for 2027
content:
Secretary‑General António Guterres told the United Nations on Tuesday that “the need for the United Nations has never been greater” as the organization confronts climate disruption, an AI revolution, war and growing hunger.

Guterres presented a programme budget proposal of $3.3 billion for the next year, which represents a reduction of $40.8 million from the previous level. The slimmer budget reflects the agency’s effort to align resources with the expanding challenges it faces.
summary: Secretary-General António Guterres said the need for the United Nations has never been greater amid climate disruption, an AI revolution, war and growing hunger. He presented a programme budget proposal of $3.3 billion for 2027, a cut of $40.8 million.
author: UN News

title: UN agency says fewer West African migrants reach Europe by sea, journey still unsafe
content:
Fewer people from West Africa are reaching Europe by sea, but the journey has not become safer, the UN migration agency (IOM) said on Tuesday.

The IOM noted that despite the decline in the number of migrants attempting the crossing, the risks associated with the sea voyage remain unchanged.
summary: The UN migration agency (IOM) said fewer people from West Africa are reaching Europe by sea. It added that the journey has not become safer.
author: UN News

title: UNDP warns 800 million young people in developing economies risk unemployment
content:
The head of the UN Development Programme (UNDP) warned on Tuesday that roughly 800 million young people entering the labour market in developing economies over the coming years will not find jobs unless countries act.  

The warning coincided with the agency’s launch of two initiatives aimed at boosting investment and employment.  

These initiatives are intended to address the projected employment gap for young people in developing economies.
summary: The head of the UN Development Programme (UNDP) warned on Tuesday that about 800 million young people entering the labour market in developing economies will not find jobs unless countries act. The agency also launched two initiatives to boost investment and employment.
author: UN News

title: UN says Taiz faces devastating humanitarian crisis as tensions raise food prices
content: Yemen’s southwestern city of Taiz is confronting a “devastating” humanitarian crisis amid a Houthi siege, a cholera outbreak and cuts to aid, the UN Spokesperson said on Tuesday. Escalating tensions are dramatically driving up food prices and causing shortages of supplies in the city. The combined pressures are putting civilians in the crosshairs of the crisis.
summary: The UN spokesperson said on Tuesday that Yemen’s southwestern city of Taiz is facing a devastating humanitarian crisis. Escalating tensions are dramatically driving up food prices and causing shortages of supplies.
author: UN News

title: Joni Mitchell, 82, becomes U.S. citizen after 62‑year journey
content:
Canada‑born singer‑songwriter Joni Mitchell, 82, announced she has become a United States citizen. The milestone follows her move to the United States in the mid‑1960s.

Mitchell shared video of her naturalisation ceremony on Instagram, accompanied by a photo beside an American flag and the caption, “A journey that began 62 years ago.” The new status grants her the right to vote in U.S. elections, a privilege she previously said she was unable to exercise.
summary: Canada‑born singer‑songwriter Joni Mitchell, 82, posted Instagram footage of her U.S. citizenship ceremony. The ceremony, following her move to the United States in the mid‑1960s, now allows her to vote in U.S. elections.
author: Guardian World

title: German authorities scramble fighter jets after false hijack alert on Corfu‑Nuremberg flight
content: A radio glitch triggered a false hijack alert, prompting German authorities to scramble fighter jets. The alert came after a pilot sent a hijack signal while flying a plane from Corfu to Nuremberg. Fighter jets were deployed to escort the aircraft as a precaution. The incident was later identified as a false alarm caused by the radio malfunction.
summary: Authorities scrambled fighter jets to escort a plane traveling from Corfu to Nuremberg. The scramble was triggered by a pilot’s hijack alert that was later found to be caused by a radio glitch.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Albanian students clash with police over education costs, university conditions and jobs
content:
Albanian students clashed with police while demonstrating against high education costs, poor university conditions and bleak job prospects.  

The confrontations occurred as the students protested what they described as inadequate funding for higher education and limited employment opportunities after graduation.
summary: Albanian students clashed with police while protesting education costs, poor university conditions and bleak job prospects. The protests highlighted concerns about high education expenses, inadequate university facilities and limited employment opportunities.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Japanese journalist Imai Yuki arrested on Sakhalin for alleged spying on Russian defence
content:
Japanese journalist Imai Yuki was detained on Russia’s Sakhalin island after the Federal Security Service (FSB) accused her of spying on Russian defence capabilities.  

The FSB said the arrest was made on suspicion of gathering intelligence related to Russia’s military.
summary: Japanese journalist Imai Yuki was arrested on Sakhalin. The FSB says the arrest was for allegedly spying on Russian defence capabilities.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Trump announces massive oil, gas and mineral exploration plan for Greenland
content: US President Donald Trump announced on his Truth Social platform a plan to pursue oil, gas and mineral exploration in Greenland. The proposal, described by Trump as “massive,” calls for increased resource development activities on the Arctic island. No further details on timelines, partners or funding were provided in the announcement.
summary: US President Donald Trump announced a plan on Truth Social for massive resource exploration in Greenland. The plan includes oil, gas and mineral exploration.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Iran increases Hormuz surveillance as ship attacks surge and oil flows fall
content: Iran has increased surveillance of the Strait of Hormuz amid a surge in attacks on vessels. According to the report, ships in the waterway are facing the worst spate of attacks since the start of the war, prompting heightened monitoring by Iranian authorities. The escalation in attacks has coincided with a renewed crash in oil flows through the strategic passage.
summary: Iran has stepped up surveillance of the Strait of Hormuz. Ships in the strait are facing the worst spate of attacks since the start of the war and oil flows have crashed again.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Kyiv says Starlink restrictions hamper front‑line operations in Ukraine
content:
Kyiv says that recent restrictions on Starlink are hampering front‑line operations in Ukraine.  

According to the statement, Elon Musk’s satellite system enables Kyiv to protect Ukrainian skies and to effectively guide drones toward Russian targets.  

The city’s officials argue that limiting access to the service undermines these defensive and offensive capabilities.
summary: Kyiv reports that restrictions on Starlink are affecting front‑line operations. The system enables Kyiv to protect Ukrainian skies and guide drones to Russian targets.
author: BBC World

title: Rams lineman Alaric Jackson suspended for punch; kicker Harrison Mevis released
content:
The Los Angeles Rams are dealing with the fallout from their recent defeat by the Buffalo Bills.  

Offensive lineman Alaric Jackson has been suspended after punching an opponent during the game.  

Kicker Harrison Mevis was released by the club following the loss.
summary: Alaric Jackson, an offensive lineman for the Los Angeles Rams, was suspended for punching an opponent. Harrison Mevis, the Rams' kicker, was released by the club.
author: BBC Sport

title: Trump says Taiwan to buy 30% of Alaska pipeline gas for 20 years
content:
President Trump announced on Tuesday that Taiwan has agreed to purchase 30 percent of gas from the Alaska pipeline over the next 20 years. The statement was made while he spoke at a campaign rally in Wasilla, Alaska.

Trump said Taiwan will invest $4.4 billion into the project, on top of $50 billion already committed by South Korea. The president was quick…
summary: President Trump announced that Taiwan agreed to purchase 30 percent of gas from the Alaska pipeline over the next 20 years. He said Taiwan will invest $4.4 billion in the project, adding to the $50 billion already committed by South Korea, and he made the remarks at a campaign rally in Wasilla, Alaska.
author: The Hill

title: Collins, Jackson Clash in Third Maine Senate Debate Ahead of Election
content:
Collins, Jackson duke it out in third Maine Senate debate: 3 takeaways

Republican Sen. Susan Collins (R) and Democrat Troy Jackson clashed Tuesday in their third Maine Senate debate, with just three weeks remaining until Election Day. The debate marked the third time the two senators faced off in a public forum.

The senators sparred on several topics, including the incumbent’s votes for and against the Iran war and their differing views on how to address cost‑of‑living issues. This was the third debate between the two senators.
summary: Republican Sen. Susan Collins (R) and Democrat Troy Jackson clashed in their third Maine Senate debate on Tuesday, with only three weeks left until Election Day. They debated the incumbent’s votes for and against the Iran war and their differing views on how to address cost of living issues.
author: The Hill

title: Trump pardons diesel mechanics for Clean Air Act violations at Alaska rally
content:
President Trump issued pardons at a campaign rally in Alaska on Tuesday for two diesel mechanics who had been charged with and pleaded guilty to violating the Clean Air Act.  

The president signed the pardons for Zachary Czubak and Patrick Fleming on stage at the campaign event in Wasilla after inviting them onto the stage.  

The action was taken during the rally, with Trump publicly granting the pardons to the two mechanics.
summary: President Trump pardoned two diesel mechanics, Zachary Czubak and Patrick Fleming, who had pleaded guilty to Clean Air Act violations. The pardons were signed on stage at a campaign rally in Wasilla, Alaska, on Tuesday.
author: The Hill

title: Ossoff, Collins Clash in Second Georgia Senate Debate
content:
Sen. Jon Ossoff (D) and Rep. Mike Collins (R) traded barbs during a Tuesday‑night debate in Georgia, marking the second face‑to‑face contest between the two Senate candidates. The exchange covered a range of issues, including the Jeffrey Epstein files and the 2020 election, among other topics.

Ossoff, the only Senate Democrat running for reelection in a state President Trump won in 2024, tied Collins to the administration’s controversial tariffs and war. The debate underscored the broader political divide between the candidates on key policy matters.
summary: Sen. Jon Ossoff and Rep. Mike Collins traded barbs in a Tuesday night debate, arguing over the Jeffrey Epstein files and the 2020 election. Ossoff, the only Senate Democrat running for reelection in a state President Trump won in 2024, tied Collins to the administration’s tariffs and war.
author: The Hill

title: Chris Cuomo questions Steve Bannon on accepting midterm results if Democrats win
content:
Chris Cuomo appeared on NewsNation on Tuesday to question former White House adviser Steve Bannon about his stance on the upcoming midterm elections. Cuomo asked Bannon whether he would accept the results if the Democrats were to defeat the Republicans.

Cuomo began the exchange with the line, “I want to ask you straight, here on the record,” before asking Bannon if the GOP lost key races, “will you accept the results of the….”
summary: Chris Cuomo questioned former White House adviser Steve Bannon on NewsNation about whether he would accept the outcome of the midterm elections if Democrats defeat Republicans. Cuomo began by asking if Bannon would accept the results of the elections.
author: The Hill

title: Iowa Senate candidate Ashley Hinson opposes Trump’s Russia diesel import deal
content:
Iowa Senate GOP candidate Ashley Hinson said on Tuesday that she does not support a recent agreement President Donald Trump made with Russia to import 300,000 tons of diesel to the United States and the global market.  

Hinson criticized the deal, arguing that the United States should not be making a transaction with an adversary. She added, “We need to lower gas prices in this …”.
summary: Iowa Senate GOP candidate Ashley Hinson said she does not agree with a recent deal President Trump struck with Russia to import 300,000 tons of diesel to the United States. She said the United States should not make a deal with an adversary and highlighted the need to lower gas prices.
author: The Hill

title: Hinson, Turek clash in final Iowa Senate debate
content:
Representative Ashley Hinson (R) and State Representative Josh Turek (D) engaged in a heated second and final debate on Tuesday for the open Iowa Senate seat. The candidates, who also clashed during their first debate last week, are competing in a toss-up race to fill the vacancy left by outgoing Senator Joni Ernst (R).

Election forecasters have recently shifted their assessments of the contest, reflecting the close nature of the race for the upper chamber position.
summary: Rep. Ashley Hinson (R) and state Rep. Josh Turek (D) held a heated second and final debate on Tuesday for the open Iowa Senate seat. The candidates are locked in a toss-up race for the seat held by outgoing Sen. Joni Ernst (R).
author: The Hill

title: Federal court overturns Tanya Plibersek's order blocking NSW goldmine
content:
A federal court has overturned a protection order issued by former environment minister Tanya Plibersek that had stalled the McPhillamys goldmine development at Blayney in central‑west New South Wales. The order, which the company said effectively blocked the mine, was issued under section 10 of the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Heritage Protection Act in 2024.

Regis Resources challenged the order, and the court ruled that the former minister’s decision was invalid. The ruling removes the legal barrier that had prevented the goldmine from proceeding.
summary: A federal court has overturned a protection order issued by former environment minister Tanya Plibersek under Indigenous heritage legislation. The order, issued in 2024, effectively blocked the McPhillamys goldmine development at Blayney in New South Wales.
author: Guardian Environment

title: What Happens in the Brain When You Can't Stop Laughing
content:
People often wonder what happens in the brain when laughter becomes uncontrollable. The article invites readers to recall a recent experience of laughing so hard they could not stop.

It suggests that such laughter can occur even in situations where it may not have been expected or appropriate.
summary: The article asks readers to recall a recent instance of uncontrollable laughter. It suggests that this may have occurred in an inappropriate situation.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study of 20,000 Nigerians Links Drug Use, Climate Change, Poverty
content:
A new study of 20,000 Nigerians explores the links between drug use, climate change, and poverty.  

The research examines how climate change—traditionally viewed as an environmental problem—affects people when their world becomes unstable. It looks at the psychological impact on those whose livelihoods, such as farming, herding, and family provision, become impossible.  

The study highlights the broader social and mental consequences of climate instability on communities.
summary: A study of 20,000 Nigerians examines how drug use, climate change, and poverty are interconnected. It looks at how climate instability undermines farming, herding, and family provision.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Norwegian Scientists Identify Abnormal Antibodies as Possible Cause of Childhood Cancer
content:
Scientists in Norway have identified a potential new mechanism that could explain the development of cancer in children.  

The research indicates that affected children appear to produce an unusual amount of aberrant antibodies targeting the building blocks of the DNA repair machinery. These antibodies attack a diverse set of hundreds of proteins that normally identify and correct damage or errors in the genome, potentially disrupting DNA repair processes.
summary: Scientists in Norway found evidence that children produce an unusual amount of aberrant antibodies targeting the proteins that make up the DNA repair machinery. These antibodies may disrupt the repair process and contribute to the development of cancer in children.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study Finds Postmenopausal Ovaries Stay Biologically Active
content:
A new study has shown that ovaries remain biologically active long after menopause. Researchers at Northwestern University and the Buck Institute for Research on Aging examined ovaries from 28 women and found that the postmenopausal ovary is not defunct.

The ovaries continued to remodel with age, displaying increased inflammation and changes in tissue structure. These findings suggest that the organ remains functionally active decades after menopause.

The study also identified a molecular link between ovarian aging and cancer.
summary: Scientists at Northwestern University and the Buck Institute for Research on Aging studied ovaries from 28 women and found that postmenopausal ovaries remain biologically active and remodel with age, showing increased inflammation and tissue changes. The study also identified a molecular link between ovarian aging and cancer.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Heathrow boss warns not building third runway would be huge missed opportunity
content:
Heathrow boss Thomas Woldbye told the BBC’s Today programme that it would be “good to know” the government’s position on the third‑runway project, following comments made by the prime minister.

Woldbye said that not building a third runway would be a “huge missed opportunity,” urging clarity from the government on the future of the expansion.
summary: Thomas Woldbye warned that not building a third runway would be a huge missed opportunity. He told the Today programme it would be good to know the government's position on the project after the prime minister's comments.
author: BBC Business

title: Cornell professor seeks data on Black women‑owned food businesses
content:
Black women in food industries face systemic roadblocks

Lilly Jan, an assistant teaching professor in the Cornell Nolan School of Hotel Administration at the Cornell SC Johnson College of Business, reported feeling perplexed and a little annoyed during her research.  

Last year, Jan was attempting to gather information on food industry businesses owned by Black women.
summary: Lilly Jan, an assistant teaching professor at Cornell Nolan School of Hotel Administration in the Cornell SC Johnson College of Business, was collecting data on food industry businesses owned by Black women. She was perplexed and a little annoyed by the difficulty of finding this information.
author: Phys.org

title: Wild bobwhite quail spotted at UT Ames AgResearch Center after habitat restoration
content:
Wild bobwhite quail were recently sighted in multiple coveys at the University of Tennessee’s Ames AgResearch and Education Center. The sightings mark an encouraging milestone in the center’s ongoing effort to restore habitat for the species.

The quail were observed at the historic bird‑dog field trial destination, indicating progress in the project’s habitat restoration goals.
summary: Multiple coveys of wild bobwhite quail were recently sighted at the University of Tennessee's Ames AgResearch and Education Center. The sighting marks a milestone in the ongoing effort to restore habitat for the species at this historic bird dog field trial destination.
author: Phys.org

title: 210‑million‑year‑old dinosaur from Zimbabwe reveals distinct prehistoric ecosystem
content:
A dinosaur fossil dated to 210 million years ago has been identified in Zimbabwe, offering new insight into Africa’s ancient ecosystems.  

Scientists say the find reveals a surprisingly distinct prehistoric environment in the region. The evidence points to ancient climate differences that may have isolated dinosaur populations across southern Africa, fostering unique species.  

The discovery challenges earlier assumptions about how these dinosaurs evolved and how their habitats were distributed.
summary: A newly identified 210‑million‑year‑old dinosaur from Zimbabwe is helping scientists uncover a surprisingly distinct prehistoric ecosystem. The discovery suggests that ancient climate differences may have separated dinosaur populations across southern Africa, leading to unique species that challenge previous assumptions about their evolution.
author: Science Daily

title: Hot planet 320 ly away shares host star chemistry, confirming formation theory
content:
Astronomers have discovered a scorching‑hot planet located 320 light‑years from Earth that shares a striking chemical similarity with its host star, confirming a long‑standing assumption about how planets form.

The finding provides the first direct evidence for that fundamental assumption and could enable scientists to predict the composition of distant rocky planets and to identify worlds with conditions favorable for life.
summary: Astronomers have discovered that a scorching-hot planet 320 light‑years away shares a striking chemical similarity with its host star. The finding provides the first direct evidence for a fundamental assumption about planet formation and could help scientists predict the makeup of distant rocky planets and identify worlds with conditions favorable for life.
author: Science Daily

title: Study finds people see AI as less conscious than humans even when behavior matches
content:
A new study finds that people maintain a sharp distinction between human consciousness and artificial intelligence even when the two behave identically. Researchers observed that participants rated the most responsive AI as less conscious than the least responsive human participant.

When the same behaviors were evaluated using the term “awareness” instead of “consciousness,” respondents judged humans and AI much more similarly. The results suggest that the language used to describe mental states strongly influences how people perceive the consciousness of machines.
summary: The study found participants rated even the most responsive AI as less conscious than the least responsive human. When asked about “awareness,” participants judged humans and AI much more similarly.
author: Science Daily

title: AI uncovers hidden shortcut in CO2-to-fuel chemistry, revealing 10,000 reactions
content:
Scientists employing artificial intelligence have identified almost 10,000 chemical reactions that convert carbon dioxide into fuels and chemicals, exposing pathways that conventional models failed to capture. The AI‑driven analysis highlighted a previously hidden shortcut in the reaction network, markedly enhancing the accuracy of CO₂ conversion predictions.

Among the newly uncovered routes, a surprising hydrogen‑based reaction stood out, offering a potential blueprint for designing more efficient catalysts. Researchers say the findings could guide future efforts to develop catalytic processes that turn CO₂ into usable fuel.
summary: Scientists used artificial intelligence to identify nearly 10,000 chemical reactions that convert carbon dioxide into fuels and chemicals. The finding improved CO2 conversion predictions and revealed a surprising hydrogen reaction that may guide more efficient catalysts.
author: Science Daily

title: New knee arthritis treatment provides lasting pain relief without surgery
content:
A new non‑surgical therapy for knee arthritis has shown the ability to provide lasting pain relief, according to a recent clinical study. The treatment employs tiny, dissolvable particles that block abnormal blood vessels in the knee, reducing inflammation and pain without the need for joint replacement surgery.

The study evaluated 194 patients who received the particle‑based injection. Eighty percent of participants reported clinically meaningful pain relief that persisted for at least 12 months after treatment. Researchers attribute the sustained benefit to the particles’ targeted action on the abnormal vasculature that contributes to arthritis symptoms.
summary: The treatment uses tiny, dissolvable particles to block abnormal blood vessels, reducing inflammation and pain without joint replacement surgery. In a study of 194 patients, 80% reported clinically meaningful pain relief lasting at least 12 months.

title: Prehistoric snake Vasuki indicus discovered in India could have been 50 ft long
content:
A massive prehistoric snake uncovered in India has been named Vasuki indicus and may have been one of the largest snakes ever known.  

The 47‑million‑year‑old fossil indicates the animal could have reached lengths of up to 50 feet, putting it on a scale comparable to the legendary Titanoboa.  

Scientists say the snake’s enormous body would have made it a slow‑moving ambush predator, a hunting style similar to that of modern anacondas.
summary: Scientists have identified a 47‑million‑year‑old snake named Vasuki indicus in India that could have reached up to 50 feet long. They believe its enormous body would have made it a slow‑moving ambush predator like a modern anaconda.

title: JAX researchers map endometriosis lesion microenvironment to reveal pain mechanisms
content:
People with endometriosis frequently report that their severe pelvic pain, intense period cramps, and other life-impacting symptoms are not taken seriously by doctors for years. New research from The Jackson Laboratory (JAX) aims to address this issue by providing a detailed map of the endometriosis lesion microenvironment.

The study identifies key cellular interactions within these lesions, offering new insights into the biological mechanisms behind the condition.
summary: Scientists at The Jackson Laboratory have created a detailed map of the endometriosis lesion microenvironment. This research aims to help address the years of struggle many people face in having their severe pelvic pain and other symptoms taken seriously by doctors.

title: Bigger data reveal second, third, and fourth switches controlling a gene
content: Genome-wide association studies, or GWAS, are now widely recognized as a standard tool for identifying genetic variants linked to complex traits. These studies have successfully identified loci associated with a range of conditions, including breast cancer, heart disease, and diabetes.

content: A new study led by researchers at University College London (UCL) indicates that children with intellectual disabilities experience heightened mental health difficulties when they come from disadvantaged backgrounds. The research highlights the intersection of socioeconomic disadvantage and intellectual disability as a factor in worsening mental health outcomes for these children.
summary: A new study led by UCL researchers found that children with intellectual disabilities experience greater mental health difficulties. This increased risk is specifically associated with children from a disadvantaged background.

title: Epstein-Barr virus hijacks cell repair processes to promote cancer
content:
Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is a common herpesvirus that infects most people at some point in their lives. The virus establishes a lifelong latent infection in its host, which is often asymptomatic but can also cause mild illnesses such as mononucleosis, a condition known as the "kissing disease" due to its transmission via saliva.

In rarer instances, EBV plays a critical role in the development of multiple sclerosis and is implicated in nearly 2% of all cancers.
summary: Epstein-Barr virus is a common herpesvirus that persists in hosts for life, often causing mild illnesses like mononucleosis. In rarer instances, the virus plays a critical role in multiple sclerosis and nearly 2% of all cancers.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Experimental cataract lens treats glaucoma with time-release bimatoprost
content:
New clinical trial results indicate that an experimental cataract lens can also treat glaucoma. Researchers presented these findings at the annual meeting of the American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO).

The artificial lenses feature small pads containing bimatoprost, a widely used glaucoma drug. This design allows the medication to be released gradually into the eye.

content: The Communication Workers Union (CWU) has reported that Royal Mail is losing 400 postal workers per week. The union attributes this exodus to the implementation of a new delivery system, which it claims is failing to function properly in hundreds of offices.

title: New computational model guides lighting design for aging eyes
content:
Researchers have developed a new computational model that accounts for the effects of aging on the human eye's ability to discriminate color. The model is designed to guide lighting designs that make it easier for older adults to perceive colors.

The approach also aims to preserve the expected appearance of colors for individuals with typical color vision.
summary: Researchers developed a computational model that accounts for how aging affects the eyes' ability to discriminate color. The model can guide lighting designs to help older adults perceive colors better while preserving appearance for those with typical vision.

title: Patterned X-rays map 3D chemical structures 43 times faster with fewer measurements
content:
Researchers at Bar-Ilan University and collaborating institutions have developed a new X-ray imaging technique designed to map the three-dimensional chemical composition of objects. This method addresses the challenge of determining an object's internal material structure in three dimensions, a task that is significantly more complex than standard internal imaging.

The new technique achieves a 43-fold increase in speed compared to conventional approaches. Additionally, it requires more than 97% less measurement data to produce the same chemical mapping results.
summary: Researchers at Bar-Ilan University and collaborating institutions developed a new X-ray imaging technique to map three-dimensional chemical composition. The method is 43 times faster than conventional approaches and uses more than 97% less measurement data.
author: Phys.org

title: Optical skyrmions control motion of magnetic skyrmions
content:
Magnetic skyrmions (MSks) are swirling patterns of magnetization that form inside certain magnetic materials. These structures behave like actual particles, characterized by a stable internal structure and distinct boundaries. Due to their extremely small size and the relatively low energy required to move them, MSks are considered promising information carriers for emerging technologies, including low-power memories and logic circuits.

A major goal in the field remains finding practical ways to control the motion of these magnetic skyrmions with high precision.
summary: Magnetic skyrmions are swirling magnetization patterns that act like particles and are promising for low-power information technologies. A major research goal is to find practical methods to control their motion with high precision.
author: Phys.org

title: Study links auditory precision to faster language pronunciation mastery
content: A new study published in the Journal of Experimental Psychology indicates that individuals with high auditory precision, the ability to notice fine details in sound, are more effective language learners. The research finds that these individuals master the pronunciation of new languages faster and more accurately than other learners.
summary: A study published in the Journal of Experimental Psychology found that people with high auditory precision master new language pronunciation faster and more accurately. This ability involves being better at noticing fine details in sound.

title: Isle of Wight fossil reveals Europe's first long-clawed megaraptoran dinosaur
content:
A UCL-led team has identified a new species of megaraptoran dinosaur from a fossil discovered on the Isle of Wight. Described in a paper published in the journal Royal Society Open Science, the animal is a long-clawed predator approximately the size of a large tiger.

This discovery marks the first time a member of the megaraptoran group, characterized as agile, two-legged carnivores, has been found in Europe.
summary: A UCL-led team discovered a new species of megaraptoran dinosaur from a fossil found on the Isle of Wight. This long-clawed predator, described in the journal Royal Society Open Science, is the first of its group to be identified in Europe.
author: Phys.org

title: Scientists discover giant fungus Dianjunus rex in Chinese forests
content:
Scientists have identified a new fungal species named Dianjunus rex in the forests of Yunnan, China, marking a significant find in mycology. This "fungal giant" is distinguished by its vertical fruiting bodies, which can reach heights of up to 50 cm (20 inches) and weigh as much as 2.2 kg (4.9 pounds).

The discovery challenges existing understandings of fungal size, as Dianjunus rex is the largest known species within the phylum Ascomycota. The fungus possesses a unique lineage that dates back approximately 65 million years.
summary: Scientists have discovered a new fungal species named Dianjunus rex in the forests of Yunnan, China. This fungus produces vertical fruiting bodies up to 50 cm high and weighing 2.2 kg, making it the largest known within the phylum Ascomycota.
author: Phys.org

title: Ultrashort laser pulses measure Berry curvature in single-layer tungsten diselenide
content: Researchers at Friedrich Schiller University Jena and the University of Regensburg have developed a new method to determine the Berry curvature of electrons using light. This quantum property, which describes specific geometric characteristics of electron states, has previously been difficult to access. The team utilized ultrashort laser pulses to perform these measurements on a single atomic layer of the semiconductor tungsten diselenide. The findings were recently published in the journal Nature Photonics.
summary: Researchers at Friedrich Schiller University Jena and the University of Regensburg developed a method to determine the Berry curvature of electrons using ultrashort laser pulses. They measured this property in a single-atom-thick layer of tungsten diselenide, and the results were published in Nature Photonics.

title: Pulse Local: Mac budgeting app runs AI models locally
content:
Niz has launched Pulse Local, a budgeting application for Apple Silicon Macs that utilizes artificial intelligence models running entirely on the user's machine. The app operates in a local mode that requires no account, ensuring that the financial ledger and user queries remain on the device without transmitting analytics or crash logs. Users can import bank transactions via CSV files in any currency to access a budgeting assistant built on a fine-tuned Qwen3 0.6B model.

The application’s architecture relies on code rather than the AI model to perform financial calculations against the imported ledger. To verify accuracy, a separate 4B parameter checker model double-checks each monetary response; if the two models disagree, the app indicates uncertainty rather than providing a potentially incorrect answer. According to the developer, this verification process reduced the rate of wrong answers from approximately one in five to five in 494 across the last three tests.

Pulse Local is available for free, with an optional "Connected mode" called Sync Pass costing $29 per year to synchronize US bank accounts through Plaid. While the initial download requires approximately 2.9 GB of models and money answers take 12 to 14 seconds with the checker enabled, the app currently supports only English and Mac platforms. The developer has made the model weights available on Hugging Face and is seeking feedback on incorrect answers and unhandled questions, with Windows support planned for the future.
summary: Pulse Local is a free budgeting app for Mac Apple Silicon that processes spending queries using local AI models without sending data to external servers. The app uses a fine-tuned Qwen3 0.6B model to interpret questions, while a 4B checker model verifies financial answers to reduce errors.

title: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman Criticizes AI Doomsday Warnings at TechCrunch Disrupt
content:
Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman took the stage at TechCrunch Disrupt to address AI leaders who are issuing doomsday warnings.  

Feldman urged those warning about AI’s risks to “maybe stop talking,” arguing that the industry’s focus on potential dangers is drowning out its benefits.  

He made these remarks during the TechCrunch Disrupt event.

title: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman predicts personal AI assistants will become household staples
content:
Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman said the market is moving toward a future in which personal AI assistants are as common as household appliances.  

Feldman predicts these assistants will operate through a hybrid model, with some processing performed on local devices and additional functions handled in the cloud.  

He indicated that this shift could soon make personal AI assistants a standard feature in homes.
summary: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman says personal AI assistants will soon be as common as household appliances. He says they will operate partly on local devices and partly in the cloud.

title: Science Corporation implants vision‑restoring chip in first Stargardt disease patient
content:
Science Corporation announced that it has implanted its vision‑restoring chip in its first patient with Stargardt disease. The milestone marks the company’s initial clinical deployment of the device, which is designed to restore sight for individuals affected by the retinal condition.

At TechCrunch Disrupt, Max Hodak, former president and co‑founder of Neuralink, detailed how his company’s work with PRIMA is part of its path toward a novel brain‑computer interface (BCI). summary: Science Corporation implanted its vision‑restoring chip in its first Stargardt disease patient. Max Hodak, former president and co‑founder of Neuralink, detailed his company's work with PRIMA at TechCrunch Disrupt as part of a novel brain‑computer interface effort.

content:
OpenAI announced that it had discovered a hidden recording device in one of its offices. The San Francisco‑based AI company said the gadget was “sophisticated” and had been found during a routine security review.

The company referred the matter to the FBI and has reported that one of its employees has been arrested. In a statement issued on Tuesday, OpenAI explained that it used one of its own models to analyze the device and determine its origin.

title: Ukrainian bombings of Yandex data centres linked to drop in pro‑Russian online content
content:
Ukrainian bombings of Russian data centres owned by Yandex have sparked claims among internet users that pro‑Russian and far‑right populist content on social media has sharply declined. The users attribute the reduction to the strikes cutting off Russian disinformation “bots.”  

The article examines this claim in this edition of Truth or Fake.

title: French investigators chase hackers who seized supermarket cooling units
content:
French investigators on Tuesday were hunting the hackers who seized control of cooling units at hundreds of supermarkets in a cyberattack that highlighted vulnerabilities of connected systems, with no group publicly claiming responsibility.

FRANCE 24’s Sharon Gaffney interviewed Marta Rybczynska, a cybersecurity expert at Ygreky, who said that basic measures such as regularly updating software or passwords are essential to prevent hacking attacks.

No group has claimed responsibility.
summary: French investigators are hunting the hackers who seized control of cooling units at hundreds of supermarkets in a cyberattack. Cybersecurity expert Marta Rybczynska of Ygreky said basic measures such as regularly updating software or passwords are essential to prevent hacking attacks.

title: China expands auto production capacity in Europe, partnering with local firms
content:
China is shifting from exporting cars to establishing full auto‑industry ecosystems in Europe, building production capacity and strengthening partnerships with local companies.  

Philipp Seidel, an automotive expert at Arthur D. Little, told France 24 that while tariffs and quotas can buy time, EU carmakers must improve their own competitiveness and avoid becoming overly dependent on Chinese suppliers.  

The article also notes that the latest IMF global growth forecast includes a warning about rising debt.

title: Pope Leo XIV has cancerous lung growth removed in 90‑minute surgery
content:
Pope Leo XIV underwent a 90‑minute lung operation on Tuesday, during which a cancerous growth was removed from his right lung, the Vatican said. The procedure was described as radical, with the lower lobe of the right lung removed to ensure complete removal of the tumor.

After the operation, the Pope “woke up normally,” according to the Vatican statement. A Vatican source added that further tests are being carried out to determine whether the cancer has spread.

The information was reported by Seema Gupta of France 24 from Rome.
summary: Pope Leo XIV underwent a 90‑minute operation on Tuesday in which a cancerous growth was removed from the lower lobe of his right lung. He woke up normally and the Vatican said further tests are being conducted to determine if the cancer has spread.

title: Arsenal 3-0 Lille, Atletico Madrid 2-0 Manchester United in Champions League
content:
Arsenal scored three goals in seven second‑half minutes on Tuesday to beat Lille 3‑0, keeping their perfect start in the Champions League intact.  

Atletico Madrid defeated Manchester United 2‑0, a result that deepens the pressure on Michael Carrick.  

Bayern Munich were held to a shock 3‑3 draw by Norway’s Viking after Michael Olise was sent off.

title: Russian missile hits Kyiv power plant, killing at least two, no warning from allies
content:
Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky announced on Tuesday that a Russian ballistic missile struck a Kyiv power plant without any advance warning from Western allies. The strike killed at least two people and wounded about 20.

The attack occurred days after U.S. President Donald Trump announced an energy ceasefire between Moscow and Kyiv. The incident has raised questions over efforts to halt strikes on critical infrastructure.
summary: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said a Russian ballistic missile struck a Kyiv power plant without advance warning from Western allies, killing at least two people and wounding around 20. The attack occurred days after US President Donald Trump announced an energy ceasefire between Moscow and Kyiv, raising questions about efforts to halt strikes on critical infrastructure.

title: Mauritius imposes curfew after protests over police shooting of 27-year-old woman
content:
Mauritius imposed a curfew following a night of unrest triggered by a police shooting. The authorities acted after demonstrators blocked roads and set tyres alight in protest of the incident.

The unrest was sparked by the shooting of a 27‑year‑old woman by police, prompting the road blockades and tyre fires that led officials to enforce the curfew.
summary: Mauritius has imposed a curfew after a night of unrest over a police shooting. Protesters blocked roads and burned tyres in response to the shooting of a 27-year-old woman.

content: Bayern Munich’s UEFA Champions League match against Viking finished in a 3‑3 draw, but the game was marked by Michael Olise’s dismissal after receiving two yellow cards within seconds. content:
Ex‑gang leader Duane “Keffe D” Davis was sentenced to 40 years to life for the 1996 murder of rapper Tupac Shakur.

summary: Duane 'Keffe D' Davis, a former gang leader, was sentenced to a term of 40 years to life for the 1996 murder of rapper Tupac Shakur. The sentencing concludes a 30‑year search for justice and follows Davis’s own writings about the shooting.

content: US authorities arrested a Saudi national who works as an OpenAI engineer after a listening device was discovered in a meeting room. The individual was charged with allegedly planting the concealed surveillance device. The case remains under investigation by U.S. officials.

content:

title: The Chicks Celebrate Taking the Long Way at Beacon Theatre Anniversary Show
content:
The Chicks performed the second of three sold-out concerts at New York’s Beacon Theatre on Monday night, celebrating the 20th anniversary of their album Taking the Long Way. The show marked two decades since the country music industry effectively blacklisted the trio following their protest of the Iraq War.

The controversy originated in March 2003, eight days before the US invasion of Iraq, when lead singer Natalie Maines stated on stage in London that she was “ashamed” President George W. Bush was from the band’s home state of Texas. This comment, which circulated on AM radio and cable news, triggered a swift backlash that included CD-burning protests and death threats against the group.

Audience members at the Beacon Theatre reflected on where they were during that period, with many noting they were in high school. The article’s author, who was nine years old at the time, recalled how the band’s popularity vanished overnight, with hits like Travelin’ Soldier, Landslide, and Cowboy Take Me Away disappearing from radio playlists.
summary: The Chicks performed at New York's Beacon Theatre to mark the 20th anniversary of their album Taking the Long Way and the backlash following lead singer Natalie Maines' 2003 comments about the Iraq War. The trio played the second of three sold-out shows, reflecting on the CD-burning protests and death threats they faced after criticizing the conflict.

title: Lena Dunham’s Girls to Return for Five-Episode HBO Revival in 2027
content:
HBO has announced that the series Girls will return for a limited five-episode run in 2027. This revival marks a reunion of the cast and crew approximately a decade after the original series finale aired, with production scheduled to begin next year.

Creator and star Lena Dunham will reprise her role as aspiring writer Hannah Horvath. She will be joined by Allison Williams as Marnie Michaels, Zosia Mamet as Shoshanna, Jemima Kirke as Jessa, and Andrew Rannells as Elijah. Judd Apatow is also set to return to the project as an executive producer.
summary: The HBO series Girls will return for a limited five-episode run in 2027, with production set to begin next year. Creator and star Lena Dunham will reunite with Allison Williams, Zosia Mamet, Jemima Kirke, and Andrew Rannells for the revival.

content: Katie Price has denied having "any venom" toward her ex-husband, Kieran Hayler, as he faces a rape trial. Hayler is currently on trial, denying offences against a girl when she was 13. The couple were married at the time the alleged offences occurred.

content:
Matt Richardson has pledged to cooperate with a British Cycling investigation into allegations of serious misconduct following his withdrawal from the Track Cycling World Championships in Shanghai. summary: Matt Richardson has promised to cooperate with a British Cycling investigation into allegations of serious misconduct. He was withdrawn from the Track Cycling World Championships in Shanghai after the allegations were reported.

title: England defeat Greece 5-0 to set up World Cup playoff final against Ukraine
content:
Lauren James scored twice and provided an assist in a dominant four-goal first half, while Alessia Russo and Georgia Stanway also found the net as England defeated Greece 5-0 in the second leg of their playoff semi-final. The victory gave England an aggregate score of 8-1, securing their place in the playoff final against Ukraine.

Russo, who is teammates with James and Stanway at Arsenal, scored her goals in the 75th minute and either side of the break, while James added her two goals in the 16th and 34th minutes. Stanway contributed to the scoring in the 30th minute as the Lionesses delivered a clinical performance against Greece.

This result sets up a playoff final against Ukraine in November and December, with England now two games away from securing their spot at the World Cup.
summary: Lauren James scored two goals and Alessia Russo scored twice in England's 5-0 victory over Greece in the playoff semi-final second leg. The win secures a playoff final match against Ukraine for England in November and December.

title: Saka and Timber secure Arsenal win against Lille to extend winning streak
content:
Arsenal secured their twelfth consecutive victory in the Champions League, defeating a resilient Lille side at the Emirates Stadium. The match served as a tribute to Ken Friar, the club’s life president who played a key role in the team’s 2006 relocation from Highbury to the Emirates.

Bukayo Saka, entering as a supersub, scored the third goal of the match to seal the win for Mikel Arteta’s team. This goal marked the 36th Arsenal has scored at the Emirates in the league or group stage of the Champions League since their return to Europe’s top tier three years ago.
summary: Bukayo Saka scored the third goal in Arsenal's victory over Lille, extending their winning streak to twelve matches. The win marked Arsenal's 36th goal at the Emirates in the Champions League league or group stage since returning to Europe's top table under Mikel Arteta.

title: Barrios scores after 53 seconds as Atlético beat 10-man Manchester United 2-0
content:
Manchester United suffered a 2-0 defeat against Atlético Madrid, with Pablo Barrios scoring just 53 seconds into the match. Manager Michael Carrick had previously stated that his players were ready to embrace the challenge and expected a reaction, but the team instead recorded another loss during a season that has seen them post their worst start in 40 years.

Ademola Lookman added a second goal late in the game to secure the victory for Atlético. United also saw Leny Yoro receive a red card in the 79th minute while the score was 1-0, though the article notes that this late dismissal may not fully mitigate the team's overall performance. The defeat highlighted a sense of resignation among the players, as the match began poorly, failed to improve, and ended with a significant loss.
summary: Pablo Barrios scored after 53 seconds and Ademola Lookman added a late goal to secure a 2-0 victory for Atlético over Manchester United. Manchester United finished the match with 10 men after Leny Yoro received a red card while the score was 1-0.

title: Trump administration asks court to revisit offshore wind farm approval
content:
The Trump administration has asked a federal court to reconsider a prior approval of a nearly‑completed offshore wind farm. The request marks a further escalation in the administration’s challenges to wind‑energy projects.

The move has raised questions about an infrastructure deal with Democrats, as the administration’s scrutiny of wind projects has intensified. The request is part of a broader pattern of the administration’s attacks on wind energy.

On Friday, the administration filed a motion with Judge Roy Lamberth, asking the court to allow it to reassess whether its past approval of the wind farm was appropriate.

content:
House Foreign Affairs Committee Democrats urged further accountability after the White House announced on Tuesday that the Trump administration had asked U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign amid reports of alleged misconduct.

content: Mark Zandi, chief economist at Moody’s Analytics, stated on Monday that the war in Iran has cost the average American household $2,000 so far. content:

content:

The bill also seeks to dismantle the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and replace it with a new “community-centered” department.

content: The Trump administration published a new rule on Tuesday that accelerates the process for terminating a refugee’s status, permitting the revocation to occur in as little as 10 days. content:

content:

content: A fusion-loop-engineered vaccine designed to protect against the Zika virus (ZIKV) has demonstrated promise in a nonhuman primate model. This approach aims to separate Zika protection from the risk of worsening dengue. The findings were published in Cell Reports Medicine on Oct. 7.

title: VIB stem-cell model shows shared origin for tissue-resident macrophages
content:
Researchers at VIB have developed a new human stem-cell-based model that recreates an early stage of immune-cell development. This model demonstrates how a single progenitor population can give rise to specialized macrophages across different organs.

The platform allows for the study of how these developmental processes change in disease. It also provides a basis for exploring how these mechanisms might eventually be harnessed therapeutically.
summary: VIB researchers developed a human stem-cell-based model that recreates early immune-cell development. The model demonstrates how a single progenitor population gives rise to specialized macrophages across different organs.

title: Yo-yo dieting risk varies with starting weight, study finds
content:
A recent article in Nature Reviews Endocrinology presents an assessment by DZD researchers Norbert Stefan and Faidon Magkos of the University of Copenhagen on the health effects of repeated weight loss and regain.

The researchers argue that the impact of weight fluctuations depends on the starting weight. They report that weight swings appear to be less problematic for people with obesity than is often assumed, whereas for individuals of normal weight the pattern could raise the long‑term risk of developing obesity.

The assessment was offered by DZD researchers Norbert Stefan and Faidon Magkos of the University of Copenhagen.
summary: Researchers Norbert Stefan and Faidon Magkos from the University of Copenhagen examined the health impact of yo‑yo dieting in a Nature Reviews Endocrinology article. They found that weight fluctuations are less problematic for people with obesity but may increase the long‑term risk of obesity in people of normal weight.

title: Robotic surgery proves effective and safe for hard-to-reach side abdominal hernias
content:
Surgeons have demonstrated that robotic technology can effectively and safely repair a rare type of hernia that develops along the side of the abdomen.  

The hernias are considered hard to treat because they form near the ribs, pelvis, muscles, nerves and blood vessels, making conventional approaches challenging.  

The use of robotic surgery therefore offers a viable solution for addressing these difficult‑to‑reach abdominal hernias.
summary: Surgeons have shown that robotic technology can help repair a rare and difficult type of hernia that develops along the side of the abdomen. These hernias are hard to treat because they form near the ribs, pelvis, muscles, nerves and blood vessels.

title: Cleveland Clinic study links alcohol brain damage to microglia
content:
A research team at Cleveland Clinic has identified a new mechanism by which alcohol abuse leads to brain dysfunction and damage. The study reveals that this process occurs through immune cells known as microglia.

The research findings also point to a potential new target for treating alcohol-related brain issues.
summary: Cleveland Clinic researchers found that alcohol abuse causes brain dysfunction and damage through immune cells called microglia. The study also identified a potential new treatment target for this condition.

However, SiC generally requires high‑temperature processing, and simultaneously forming and controlling porous structures at the nanometer scale remains challenging.

title: Carpet growth method yields long-sought 2D quantum material
content:
The Carpet' growth method has produced a long‑sought two‑dimensional quantum material, a topological insulator that physicists have been searching for for decades.  

This ultrathin material blocks electricity in its interior while conducting along its edges. In ordinary wires, electrons constantly bounce off imperfections and lose energy. In the 2D topological insulator, electrons with opposite spins travel in opposite directions along the edges—like cars in one‑way lanes—so they rarely scatter and lose energy.
summary: The new 2D topological insulator blocks electricity in its interior while conducting along its edges. Electrons with opposite spins travel in opposite directions along the edges, reducing scattering and energy loss.

title: Parsimony: Open-Source Benchmark Measures Excess Code Added by AI Models
content:
A new open-source benchmark called Parsimony has been introduced to evaluate the amount of code AI models generate, addressing a gap in existing metrics that typically focus on solve rates and token costs. The tool aims to quantify how much excess code is added, a factor that can complicate long-term project maintenance.

Parsimony operates by analyzing patches from established benchmarks, including DeepSWE, SWE-bench Verified, and SWE-bench Live. It calculates "coding units"—syntax elements such as statements, calls, names, and literals—rather than lines of code, which prevents models from gaining advantage by cramming code. The metric measures net units by subtracting deleted code from added code.

For models GPT-6 and Claude 5.5, which do not yet have public patches available, the developer ran them on 3–10 tasks using personal subscriptions. These results are displayed as faded circles and are not included in the main ranking. The project is hosted on GitHub and is not affiliated with the source benchmarks, with the developer inviting feedback and public patch exports for newer models.
summary: Parsimony is an open-source benchmark that evaluates AI models by counting "coding units" in patches from existing benchmarks to measure net code added. It uses syntax elements rather than lines of code to avoid rewarding cramped code, and includes self-run results for GPT-6 and Claude 5.5.

The legislation, described as sweeping, now moves to the Senate, where supporters warn its key provisions could be diluted despite the government’s pledge to safeguard the bill’s ambition.

Eight political groups, ranging from the Communists to Les Républicains (LR), sponsored the text, which was adopted with 503 votes in favor and none against. Deputies from La France Insoumise (LFI) abstained, criticizing the removal of measures intended to protect foreign women. FRANCE 24’s Monte Francis reported.
summary: The National Assembly overwhelmingly approved the “comprehensive” bill against sexist and sexual violence with a vote of 503 to 0. Sponsored by eight political groups from the Communists to Les Républicains (LR), the bill now goes to the Senate, and LFI (La France Insoumise) deputies abstained, denouncing the removal of measures protecting foreign women.

title: Duane Davis sentenced to minimum 40 years for Tupac Shakur killing
content:

Davis had previously boasted in books and interviews about his role in the murder, but denied the allegations when he appeared at trial.

title: Saudi Arabia faces Houthi attacks on airports and energy facilities
content:

The attacks have prompted questions about the viability of a Saudi‑led international military offensive against the Houthi militia in Yemen. Analysts are weighing whether such an operation could succeed in countering the militia’s growing capabilities.

content:

content:

title: California coastal homes battered by intense waves and flooding after Tropical Storm Rachel
content:
California coastal homes were battered and bruised after a weekend of intense waves and flooding. The extreme weather left flooding that overtook city streets and intense waves that battered beachside homes, with a boardwalk destroyed in Long Beach and homes damaged across the region.

The remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel hit Mexico’s Baja California over the weekend, as well as southern California and Las Vegas. Meteorologists noted that Rachel weakened into a post‑tropical cyclone as it approached California, yet it still left a trail of destruction.

Southern California coastal communities are picking up the pieces after the weekend of extreme weather.
summary: Boardwalks in Long Beach were destroyed and homes were damaged along the California coast. The remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel, which weakened into a post-tropical cyclone, caused flooding and intense waves that also affected Baja California and Las Vegas.

title: DR Congo Ebola cases exceed 9,000 amid Bundibugyo strain outbreak
content:

The outbreak, driven by the Bundibugyo strain, is the deadliest Ebola episode in the country’s history, and health workers are confronting mistrust from local communities.  

The continued spread underscores the difficulty of containing the epidemic under current conditions.
summary: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak has surpassed 9,000 cases, driven by the Bundibugyo strain. Health workers are struggling with community mistrust, hindering efforts to curb transmission.

content:

content: NASA’s Perseverance rover has set a new interplanetary driving record, becoming the farthest‑traveling robotic vehicle on a world beyond Earth. title: RJ Mitte, Breaking Bad actor, dies at 34
content:
RJ Mitte, the actor best known for playing Walter White Jr. on the television series Breaking Bad, died at the age of 34 in Brownsville, Texas.

Mitte’s personal experience living with cerebral palsy informed his portrayal of Walter White Jr., and he used his platform to advocate for disability representation and inclusion. His representatives issued a statement describing him as a beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability‑rights advocate, noting that he drew from his own condition to bring authenticity to the role.

Bryan Cranston remembered Mitte as “my sweet son,” reflecting the close bond between the two actors.
summary: Actor RJ Mitte, who played Walter White Jr. in Breaking Bad, died aged 34 in Brownsville, Texas. His representatives called him a philanthropist and disability rights advocate, noting his authenticity from living with cerebral palsy and that Bryan Cranston remembered him as “my sweet son.”

title: Netflix’s Four‑Part Tyson Documentary Features Trump Cameo and Psychedelic Scenes
content:
Netflix has released a new four‑part documentary series about former boxing champion Mike Tyson, which reviewers have called one of the strangest sports documentaries ever produced by the streaming service. The series is described as a hagiography that mixes psychedelics, sobbing, and a cameo involving a face tattoo.

The film features a cameo from U.S. President Donald Trump, who appears to defend Tyson. This appearance has been noted as a baffling choice that diverges from Trump’s usual focus on geopolitics and golf.

The final episode ends with Tyson taking the hallucinogenic drug DMT—which he refers to as “the toad”—while sobbing and inviting the show’s director to join him.
summary: Netflix released a four‑part documentary about former boxing champion Mike Tyson that includes a cameo from Donald Trump. The film ends with Tyson taking the hallucinogenic drug DMT, sobbing, and inviting the director to join him.
